Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills and is on injured reserve, shifting the line for this game from Ravens -3 (the lookahead) to Jaguars -9.5. That move also comes after backup Tyler Huntley (turf toe) was ruled out for this game and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury. So, the Ravens are in a brutal spot as they look to get back over .500 (Baltimore is 4-4 this season) against the top team in the AFC South. Jacksonville is in a great spot to win the AFC South for the second season in a row, as no other team in the division has more than two wins in 2026. The Jags blew out the Indianapolis Colts – 42-7 – in Week 8, and they’re one of the best defenses in the league, ranking third in EPA/Play and eighth in success rate. Liam Coen’s team is a deserved favorite in this matchup, which could be a tough one to bet on with all the Baltimore injuries. Still, the SI Betting team has curated some picks for Week 9’s Thursday Night showdown, including player props for Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Here’s a breakdown of some of our favorite bets for the action to kick off the final week of the first half of the 2026 season. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Jaguars vs. Ravens Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Jacksonville Jaguars -8.5 (-115) vs. Baltimore Ravens – Iain MacMillan Bhayshul Tuten Anytime TD (+115) – Peter Dewey Trevor Lawrence UNDER 31.5 Pass Attempts (-118) – Peter Dewey Derrick Henry UNDER 70.5 Rushing Yards (-109) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s taking the Jaguars to cover on the road with Baltimore dealing with some major quarterback issues: The Baltimore Ravens don't have a quarterback, which is obviously a pretty important aspect of being competitive in an NFL game. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are likely out for the game, and their third-string quarterback, Joe Fagnano, is also questionable due to an injury. If he can't go, the Ravens are going to be starting a quarterback who's not on their roster as of me writing this article on Monday night. That leaves the Ravens' only plan of attack being running the football. Unfortunately, they now have to face a Jaguars defense that ranks second in opponent rush EPA and seventh in opponent rush success rate, while giving up fewer yards per carry than any other defense in the league (3.4). I could maybe be convinced to take the points with the Ravens if they had an elite defense, but they're completely average on that side of the ball. Jaguars second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten has played a major role on offense this season, appearing in 55.3 percent of the team’s snaps while registering at least 12 carries in every game. Tuten also has six straight games with two or more receptions, finding the end zone three times through the air and four times overall in his last two games. Chris Rodriguez is also going to factor into the Jacksonville attack, but I’m buying Tuten at +115 to find the end zone on Thursday. While Baltimore is allowing just 3.8 yards per carry this season, it’s already allowed 10 rushing scores. This could be a run-heavy game script for the Jags since they’re nearly favored by double digits, and Tuten has six total scores in seven games in 2026. He should continue to see a ton of work as the Jaguars look to run away with the AFC South. A former No. 1 overall pick, Lawrence is in the MVP conversation this season, but he hasn’t been asked to throw the ball a ton with this Jaguars offense humming on the ground in 2026. Lawrence is averaging under 29 pass attempts per game in 2026, and he threw the ball just 14 times in a 42-7 win over Indianapolis in Week 8. Overall, the star quarterback has just two games (Weeks 5 and 6) where he even attempted 30 passes. So, with the Jaguars heavily favored on a short week, I expect a lighter workload for Lawrence against a Ravens team that has lost three straight and is staring down a lost season with Jackson sidelined. If this game turns into a blowout like the Colts matchup did, Lawrence may not even attempt 25 passes for the fourth time in eight games. This season, Derrick Henry has just four games with over 70 rushing yards, and he’s coming off three straight down performances with 58, 45 and 53 rushing yards, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry during that stretch. The Jaguars are going to stack the box against Henry with all of Baltimore’s quarterback issues, and Jacksonville held Jonathan Taylor to under 30 rushing yards in a blowout in Week 8. The game script isn’t going to be favorable for Henry, and he only saw 11 rushes in Week 8. Jacksonville ranks No. 1 in the NFL in EPA/Rush, allowing the fewest yards per carry (3.4) and total rushing yards (542) in the league this season. picks.headline: Ravens Slammed With Horrific Prediction Hours Before Jaguars Game
picks.blurb: Ravens Slammed With Horrific Prediction Hours Before Jaguars Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Ravens Slammed With Horrific Prediction Hours Before Jaguars Game (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) Evan Massey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 4:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens badly need to figure out how to come through with a win on Thursday Night Football to kick off Week 9 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. On the positive side, the Ravens will be playing in front of their home crowd. However, they are going to be playing without superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup signal caller Tyler Huntley. Getting the start will be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. He came into the game last week against the Buffalo Bills and made his NFL debut, completing 10 of his 21 pass attempts for 91 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. Hailing from Boston College, the 6-foot-3 and 225-pound quarterback threw for 3,448 yards, 28 touchdowns, and just one interception in 2025 with the Huskies. He completed 69 percent of his passes that year and chipped in with 131 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Behind Fagnano, the team will have Kedon Slovis as the primary backup. He was signed off of the Green Bay Packers' practice squad this week. Baltimore has made the move to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, but that trade will not finalize until later in the week. He won't be eligible to play against the Jaguars. Just hours before the game against Jacksonville kicks off, the Ravens have been slammed with a horrific prediction. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio isn't giving Baltimore any chance to knock off the 5-2 Jaguars. He is predicting that the Ravens will be defeated by a final score of 27-13. At the end of the day, Baltimore has a lot of adversity to overcome. Sometimes, teams find the best of themselves in these moments. But, there is no question that the Ravens are facing an uphill battle against one of the top contenders in the AFC. Coming into this week's game, Baltimore has lost three straight games. Following their impressive 4-1 start, the Ravens are just 4-4 at this point in time. Obviously, the team's playoff hopes are very much in danger. Baltimore's hopes of winning a Super Bowl seem all but over. No one can fully count the Ravens out, but things are looking bleak. A win over Jacksonville would be a huge step towards getting back on track. On the other hand, a fourth straight loss would put Baltimore in a very difficult situation. Kickoff tonight is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET. Fans will be able to watch the game on Prime Video.

away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.headline: Lamar Jackson told Ravens he’s coming back this season, report says
home.blurb: Injured quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return later this season, the NFL Network reported Sunday, citing anonymous sources. NFL Network reported that Jackson is undergoing surgery to repair a fractured and dislocated thumb on his right hand. Jackson’s injury typically takes at least six weeks to recover from, though it could take up to nine weeks, the report said. That would line up with a potential return during the Ravens’ four straight AFC North matchups to end the regular season, beginning Dec. 20 at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Perhaps the Ravens still have hope. “Just stay alive” was the paraphrase of Jackson’s message that he delivered within 24 hours of suffering a significant thumb injury on his throwing hand against Buffalo, the report said. After starting 4-1 with Jackson under center, Baltimore has slipped to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North, facing long odds to make the postseason. Jackson suffered the thumb injury on the offense’s first play of his first game back from an ankle injury in a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. He and backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, who suffered a season-ending turf toe injury against Buffalo, were placed on injured reserve before Thursday night’s 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , meaning they will miss at least four games. Jackson has not spoken to reporters since the injury, and coach Jesse Minter has declined to share details about it or Jackson’s potential recovery timeline. “I’m not going to speak on that,” Minter said when asked about Jackson on Thursday night. The Ravens have made plans to move forward without their two-time NFL Most Valuable Player this season, acquiring quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals last week. Though neither side disclosed the terms, Baltimore is reportedly sending Arizona a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick in exchange for the 33-year-old veteran and a 2027 fifth-round selection, ESPN reported. Brissett has started 73 of 109 games and completed 62.1% of his passes with 86 touchdowns and 39 interceptions. He also has 17 career rushing touchdowns. He is 23-50 as a starter. The move came about 12 hours after Baltimore’s embarrassing loss to the Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium, where undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his first NFL start and struggled mightily with a heavily bandaged right ankle. He completed 10 of 18 passes for just 60 yards and was intercepted twice. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The NFL returns to Spain for the second straight season with a matchup that features many of the league's top offensive stars Getty Images Following a week without an international game, the NFL heads back overseas in Week 9 when it sends the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals to Spain. The Bernabéu will play host to American football for the second time in as many years as two divisional contenders descend upon Madrid. The Bengals are in search of their first win away from American soil in franchise history after going 0-1-1 in their previous two opportunities (the most recent contest dating back to 2019), while the Falcons seek to improve to .500 in games abroad. Atlanta is 2-3 away from the United States and last season lost in Berlin. This contest pits one of the league's hottest teams against a squad that aims to reestablish positive momentum. Cincinnati rides a three-game win streak into the Madrid Game and scored no fewer than 31 points in any of those triumphs, albeit with two of the matchups coming against bottom-tier competition. Atlanta, on the other hand, lost in two of its last three outings and went scoreless in its most recent showing. Both sides are alive and well in their respective divisions, but the context between the two differs greatly. The Falcons are just a half game back of first place in the NFC South, which may be the weakest division in football with no teams at or above .500 through the season's first two months. The Bengals' position at half a game out of the AFC North lead is the superior standing considering three teams own winning records. Where to watch Falcons vs. Bengals live Date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location: Bernabéu (Madrid) TV: NFL Network, stream on fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook Falcons vs. Bengals key storylines Bijan Robinson and Drake London see bounce-back opportunity: It is no small feat to keep one of the NFL's top running back-wide receiver tandems in check, but how much credit do the Tampa Bay Buccaneers deserve for doing so in Week 8? With due respect to a formidable defense, the weather in that shutout might have had more to do with the Falcons going scoreless than anything else. A major one-week swing could be in store for this duo as it squares off against a Cincinnati unit that just allowed the Tennessee Titans to rack up 36 points. Robinson remains the league's rushing leader with 780 yards on the year, and London stands sixth in receiving yards at 624. If the Bengals could not keep the Titans in check, they will have their hands even more full with these two stars. Tee Higgins reaches new echelon: Higgins has long played second fiddle to Ja'Marr Chase in the otherworldly Bengals passing attack but is now on level ground with his superstar teammate. Both saw exactly 61 targets across their first seven games, and both grabbed 43 catches on those opportunities. But Higgins has been the far more efficient receiver of the two with 726 yards. That ranks second in the NFL, only to potential repeat Offensive Player of the Year winner Jaxon Smith-Njigba . This is the best version of Higgins the league has seen, and it is on pace for historic production . James Pearce Jr . to make season debut: The NFL reinstated Pearce after he served an eight-game suspension for a violation of the league's personal conduct policy, which makes him eligible to play for the first time this season in Week 9. Atlanta has been surprisingly disruptive on the defensive front without the second-year pass rusher, who faced felony charges this offseason following a domestic dispute but is on track to have those charges dropped. A unit that ranks sixth in quarterback pressure rate may climb even closer to the top of the leaderboard and perhaps improve its sack totals upon Pearce's insertion into the lineup, because he logged 10.5 sacks as a rookie despite starting only three games. Joe Burrow on MVP pace: Only two quarterbacks ( Josh Allen and Brock Purdy ) have shorter odds, via DraftKings Sportsbook, to win the NFL's top individual award. Burrow leads both of them in touchdowns with a league-best 20, and he is a mere 0.1 points away from the NFL lead in passer rating at 111.6. away.headline: Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives
away.blurb: Johnson was listed as questionable on the injury report with an ankle/foot designation after suffering the injury in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. Safety Kyle Dugger was ruled out Friday with the quad injury that has forced him to miss three of the last four games. Cornerback DJ Turner II injured his foot last week against the Titans and was limited to start the week, but he did not appear on the injury report and is expected to start and play his full role. Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson is active for today’s NFL International Game in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons. The other inactives are offensive tackle Myles Hinton, center Connor Lew and defensive tackle Landon Robinson. The Bengals only need four inactives today because their roster is currently at 52. The Bengals arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and practiced Thursday and Friday to get back on a normal weekly schedule. "I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," head coach Zac Taylor said on Thursday. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far." "We're back on schedule,” he added. “Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based." Quarterback Joe Burrow said he and his teammates are excited to be representing the NFL abroad and about being in a stand-alone window as the only game on Sunday morning. “It means a lot to me that we're here,” he said Friday. “I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally. I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here. "I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday." The team will fly home immediately after the game and, unlike their previous two international games when they had a bye to recover, will start preparations for a key AFC North game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers (+3) at New England Patriots This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. Pick: Bills 21, Vikings 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. The Colts also started the year 2-2, and have yet to win since Oct. 4 in Washington. They got blown out 42-7 at Jacksonville last week after a pair of closer losses. (Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Frank Ammirante · Action Network Sun, November 8, 2026 at 4:38 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys (3-5) and Indianapolis Colts (2-6) square off today in NFL Week 9. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET from Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Ind. The game will be broadcast live on FOX. The Cowboys are 4.5-point favorites on the spread (Cowboys -4.5), with the over/under set at 51.5. The Cowboys are -220 favorites on the moneyline and the Colts are +184 underdogs. Let's get into my Cowboys vs Colts predictions for Week 9. Cowboys vs Colts picks: Cowboys -5.5 (-115) | Javonte Williams Over 70.5 Rushing Yards (-114) My Cowboys vs Colts best bet is on Dallas to cover as road favorites and Javonte Williams to cover his rushing yards prop. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Cowboys vs Colts Odds Cowboys vs Colts Spread : Cowboys -4.5, Colts +4.5 Cowboys vs Colts Total : 51.5 Cowboys vs Colts Moneyline : Cowboys -220, Colts +184 Cowboys vs Colts Preview Cowboys Preview The Cowboys are coming off a disastrous loss at home against the Cardinals . In typical Cowboys fashion, they blew a 24-10 lead in the fourth quarter, only to lose 33-30 in overtime. It was a game where they struggled to run the ball, as Javonte Williams was limited to only 56 yards on 24 carries . With that said, they're in a good spot to get back on track, even though it's on the road. This is a matchup against a tanking team that is in the middle of a fire sale. Colts Preview The Colts have lost four in a row entering Week 9, fresh off a 42-7 blowout loss against the Jaguars . After trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner , this team looks demoralized. Head coach Shane Steichen is a virtual lock to be fired by the end of the season, perhaps even earlier. We're likely to see them trade both Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs as well. Even in a home game against a poorly coached Cowboys team, I prefer fading the Colts in this spot. Cowboys vs Colts Spread Pick to Make I'm taking the Cowboys -5.5 over the Colts here. We've seen the Cowboys play a lot better on the road, including wins against the Texans and Eagles . They took care of business in a game they were favored to win in Philly, when they won handily 38-21. It wouldn't surprise me to see something similar against the Colts. This is a great spot for the Cowboys offense to get rolling, as Indianapolis has allowed 42, 16, 26, and 34 points during this losing streak. In this stretch, the Colts are 23rd in Dropback EPA and 26th in Rush EPA. This may be a spot where the Cowboys can get their running game going. I like getting below the key number of six here, so we'll ride with the Cowboys -5.5 against a tanking Colts team. This is a must-win game for Dallas as they try to keep pace with the Giants in the lowly NFC East. Picks: Cowboys -5.5 (-115) Cowboys vs Colts Player Props I'm targeting the Cowboys' running game in player props, going with Javonte Williams Over 70.5 rushing yards . As I mentioned above, the Colts are 26th in Rush EPA during their four-game losing streak. We just saw Bhayshul Tuten rush for 104 yards on only 16 carries against them. Williams was inefficient against the Cardinals, but back in Week 7, he rushed for 155 yards against the Eagles, so it's not like he's been completely unproductive lately. While it's a high bar at 70.5, the Cowboys are projected to play with a lead as 5.5-point favorites, which would mean more rushing volume. Williams has a combined 49 carries in his last two games, so he's been seeing a heavy workload. That also bodes well for this prop. away.headline: Cowboys Injury Roundup: 'Tough decisions' ahead as Ferguson, Locke, others get bad news
away.blurb: FRISCO, Texas — Roughly two weeks ago, the Dallas Cowboys were feeling great about their injury report as key players began to get healthy and return to the practice and playing field. In the blink of an eye, they're suddenly back to having a lengthy and growing list of injuries that will again cost them impact players going forward. PJ Locke missed time this season before returning and suffering a concussion in Week 8, clearing protocol ahead of the matchup against the Indianapolis Colts before suffering a second concussion in as many weeks and, this time, he will not return in only a week's time. On Monday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys officially ruled Locke out of the looming contest against the San Francisco 49ers — a sign he will likely miss multiple games. It was a scary sight to see Locke lying motionless for several moments before being helped to the sideline and not being permitted to return at Lucas Oil Stadium. Turpin will join DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back), George Pickens (hamstring) and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), those three were ruled out ahead of kickoff against the Colts, in the rehab group this week to determine if either of them can go against the 49ers. And with Ferguson down, the expectation is that Luke Schoonmaker will return from injury to help with the currently ailing tight end depth chart. And though Marist Liufau was activated from injured reserve last week, Malachi Lawrence recently joined Thompson on IR, leaving the Cowboys with only one IR-DTR (designated to return) spot this regular season, assuming Lawrence returns as expected. That means if Ferguson, Goodson and Locke are moved to IR, only one of them would be allowed to return unless the Cowboys make the playoffs. In pulling out a much-needed win in Indianapolis, the Cowboys seemingly took craziness to a whole new level. After challenging his defense to execute for a full 60 minutes, Quinnen Williams led by example with a dominant performance that helped the Cowboys finish strong and close out a crucial victory. Cowboys Injury Roundup: 'Tough decisions' ahead as Ferguson, Locke, others get bad news Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Patrik Walker DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer On the offensive side of the ball, the team will be without tight end Jake Ferguson and Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks", Schottenheimer added, both nursing knee injuries suffered against the Colts. Ferguson scored the first touchdown for the Cowboys in Indy on an athletic catch before a later hit ended his afternoon, and Goodson actually returned after suffering his injury, but tests after the game revealed a very concerning issue that has yet to be disclosed. Goodson finished with 77 rushing yards on 6.7 yards per carry in Week 9, ratcheting up his impact as both RB2 and a kick returner in the absence of KaVontae Turpin (ribs). home.headline: Colts' chances of fetching anything in return for QB Daniel Jones just went up in flames following report from NFL insider
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Part of that decision likely comes down to the fact that the Colts extended Jones during the offseason. Pelissero also laid out what that contract looks like going forward. The Vikings are the team that loses out Minnesota has a Monday Night Football game this week. If Carson Wentz goes out there and stinks up the joint, the Vikings will be staring at a serious problem. Kyler Murray has been bad and is now injured, which leaves Minnesota with very few answers under center. For Colts fans, that means the rest of the season will play out with Jones as their starting quarterback. Whether that’s a comfort or a frustration probably depends on how you feel about the direction of this team. Either way, the Colts made their call, and Jones isn’t going anywhere. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Read the full story here: Colts' chances of fetching anything in return for QB Daniel Jones just went up in flames following report from NFL insider Indianapolis shut down the Daniel Jones trade chatter, and one team that badly needed a quarterback answer just lost its best option. The Indianapolis Colts lost yet another game Sunday, this time to the Dallas Cowboys . With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, the rumor mill around the NFL is spinning. Who’s going? Who’s coming? Are the Colts about to sell off everybody? Quarterback Daniel Jones , running back Jonathan Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs , and defensive tackle Grover Stewart have all come up in trade speculation. Well, we now know where Jones stands. Colts tell Daniel Jones he is staying put Tom Pelissero of The Ringer posted on that Indianapolis gave its quarterback a clear answer before the deadline: “The Colts informed quarterback Daniel Jones on Saturday They’re not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline. Teams called and the Colts listened, but they never had any intention of moving him despite speculation. Jones is staying in Indy.” The Colts' first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft belongs to the Jets; the Colts' earliest pick projects at No. 39, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Sun, Nov 8). “Daniel Jones is due $38 million in 2027 with only about $10.5 guaranteed for injury until March. That’s mid-tier quarterback money giving whoever the new GM is optionality as the rebuild begins.” That is the key detail here. Indianapolis isn’t locked into Jones long-term in a way that would hamstring a new front office. The flexibility is there, and there’s no need to rush a deal at the deadline when the decision can wait until the spring. Jones was asked about the trade rumors in his postgame interview, before Pelissero’s report surfaced. He made it clear where his loyalty lies. “I believe in Shane Steichen. I believe in what we’re doing. I love playing for Shane. So like I said, I hadn’t thought about it much. I’ve been so focused on Dallas and making sure I was ready.” That’s about as strong an endorsement of Colts head coach Shane Steichen as you’ll hear

picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Jets: NFL Week 9 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On the heels of consecutive losses to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs are back at home and have a lighter game in the 12:00 p.m. local slot against the New York Jets. Just because New York doesn't have the makings of a playoff contender doesn't mean it can't give Kansas City a fight, though. The Chiefs know as well as any team that self-inflicted errors are the easiest way to hand a game over, so the hosts will have to put the pedal to the metal in order to secure a resounding triumph. With kickoff just hours away, will it be the Chiefs or Jets that emerge with a victory? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 9 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: While there's only so much the Chiefs can truly prove against the 2-6 Jets, this is a game Kansas City simply has to win. A two-game losing streak to a pair of playoff teams is one thing. A home loss to a franchise that’s still a year away from even making the “in the hunt” playoff graphic? That would be disastrous. I’ll be watching to see if the Chiefs’ pass rush can wrangle Geno Smith, who is tied for the second-most sacks taken among quarterbacks this season, while hoping to see more from rookie R Mason Thomas in that effort. Will the Chiefs’ banged-up defense be able to hold down a lively group of weapons, even without Garrett Wilson, or will the KC offense need to score more than 24 points for the first time since before the bye week? I could see a bounce-back stat line for Kenneth Walker with another explosive play or two from the star running back. Jordan Foote: The Chiefs typically have at least one game a year they have no business losing and somehow just don't seem to show up for. While it's possible that this is the one, it absolutely cannot be the case. Coming off ugly losses to the Seahawks and Broncos (for different reasons), this is a squad that desperately needs to rebound in a hurry. Fortunately, the matchup is there in Week 9. The Jets' offense has had its shining moments, although it's virtually impossible to trust this version of Smith to go toe-to-toe with Patrick Mahomes if he's on his game. Add in that Kenneth Walker III may be due for another statement performance, and it's hard to see anything other than turnovers or penalties making this too close of a game, in my view. Tyler Brown: The Jets have been more competitive than their 2-6 record suggests, with five of their six losses coming by one score, and Geno Smith has been a pleasant surprise. They can be dangerous on offense, with wideouts Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell playing well lately and running back Breece Hall returning, even as Braelon Allen's rushed for 565 yards. This is also a real test for tackles Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore, who will face pass rushers David Bailey and Will McDonald IV. On the other hand, New York’s defense has been giving up production to opposing tight ends, which sets up Travis Kelce and Noah Gray well. Andy Reid can wear the Jets down with Kenneth Walker and, in a perfect world, let Patrick Mahomes work the secondary off that. Smith is also among the league’s worst at turning pressure into sacks, so a Chiefs pass rush that's been waiting for a game like this should hypothetically get home a few times. Neither team will run away, and the Jets will stay in it for a while. But Kansas City is the more talented team and needs the win more. The Chiefs have a stretch of must-win games ahead, and they find a way to handle this one. Published Nov 8, 2026 JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. The two AFC opponents will meet on the gridiron for the first time since 2023 as KC returns to Arrowhead Stadium following a road stretch. Kansas City will be motivated on both sides of the ball after surrendering a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter to the Broncos. Now that the Chiefs no longer hold the lead in the AFC West, every game from here on out is crucial to staying alive in the division race. Meanwhile, the Jets are merely playing for draft position at this stage of the season, having lost six of their past seven matchups and presumably looking to sell a few key pieces at the trade deadline. However, head coach Aaron Glenn is also trying to preserve his job security and convince ownership he's the right man for the job. While sportsbooks favor the Chiefs in this one, what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Here's what the computer model projects one day before kickoff. picks.blurb: Complete Chiefs Inactives for Week 9 vs. Jets: Updates on Both First-Round Picks Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI After a week to reflect on a two-game losing skid, the Kansas City Chiefs are back in action in the early window on Sunday. Coming to town are the New York Jets, who may be 2-6 but have numerous one-score losses that hint at this team being better than its record indicates. As expected while the 2026-27 NFL campaign approaches the trade deadline , neither of these clubs is close to fully healthy. Could that factor into how Week 9's game unfolds? Perhaps, especially with several high-profile players missing this weekend's contest. With that in mind, here's who's inactive for Kansas City and New York in Sunday's matchup. Kansas City Chiefs inactives vs. New York Jets Here are the Chiefs’ inactives for today’s game against New York: CB Mansoor Delane QB Garrett Nussmeier FB Ben VanSumeren DE Jack Pyburn OT Diego Pounds DT Peter Woods CB Mansoor Delane QB Garrett Nussmeier (emergency third quarterback) FB Ben VanSumeren DE Jack Pyburn OT Diego Pounds DT Peter Woods The Chiefs' injury situation was pretty bleak a week ago when a pair of cornerbacks were ruled out for an eventual defeat to the Denver Broncos. L'Jarius Sneed went on the injured reserve list , with No. 6 overall NFL Draft pick Mansoor Delane also sitting with a lingering shoulder issue. The latter injury remains a problem in Week 9, as head coach Andy Reid revealed on Friday that the star rookie would be inactive once again. In the same Friday media availability, Reid ruled defensive tackle Peter Woods out. Woods, who left Week 8's outing with a neck injury after just three snaps, didn't practice all week. Two other injury notes for the Chiefs pertain to supporting players on the depth chart. Special teams ace Nikko Remigio kicked off the week as a limited participant in practice but progressed to full participation in time to carry a questionable designation into Sunday. He's good to go. On defense, second-year tackle Omarr Norman-Lott was limited for another week and ruled out on Friday. Norman-Lott has one more week left in his 21-day evaluation window after being designated to return from the physically unable to perform list. He isn't listed among KC's inactives due to technically still not being on the active roster. On Saturday, the Chiefs activated defensive tackle Marcus Harris from the practice squad via standard elevation. New York Jets inactives vs. Kansas City Chiefs Harrison Phillips is active for #NYJvsKC WR Garrett Wilson WR Tim Patrick DB Nahshon Wright EDGE Joseph Ossai LB Trevin Wallace OL Kohl Levao OL Blake Freeland In advance of Sunday's game, the Jets ruled out multiple players. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson headlines the list, as he remains in concussion protocol and didn't practice all week. Elsewhere, players like linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin), defensive end Joseph Ossai (ankle) and cornerback Nahshon Wright (back) are also missing in action. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips, who's been battling an ankle injury, was deemed questionable after not participating in Wednesday and Thursday's practices before getting a full workload on Friday. New York is letting him give it a go in Kansas City. Published Nov 8, 2026 JORDAN FOOTE Jordan Foote covers the Kansas City Chiefs for Chiefs On SI. picks.blurb: Two Bold Predictions for the Kansas City Chiefs vs. New York Jets in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Two Bold Predictions for the Kansas City Chiefs vs. New York Jets in Week 9 Ryan L. Dodson · Athlon Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 11:16 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return home Sunday to face the New York Jets after dropping two straight games. Running back Kenneth Walker III has been bottled up in the defeats after leading the league in rushing through his first five games. The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos limited K9 to a combined 105 rushing yards on 35 carries. Bold Prediction No. 1: Running Back Kenneth Walker Tops 100 Yards The Jets have allowed the seventh-most rushing yards to opposing running backs through eight weeks. Walker topped 100 yards on the ground in four of the first five games of the season. Even after averaging just 3.0 yards per carry the last two games, he's still second in the NFL with 5.5 yards per carry. Two weeks ago, the Jets allowed Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon to rush for 103 yards on 25 carries . Walker is a clear upgrade from Gordon and will gash the Jets on the ground. The Chiefs' passing game has also had its issues. Tight end Travis Kelce has been managing an ankle injury, and they'll look to run the ball often. Bold Prediction No. 2: Chiefs Defense Records 2+ Sacks The Chiefs' pass rush has been much maligned, and it's for good reason. They're tied for last in the NFL with nine sacks on the season. Defensive tackle Chris Jones, who is one of their leading pass rushers, has just a half-sack on the season. Defensive end George Karlaftis reached the quarterback in Week 8 for his team-leading second sack of the season. The Jets are tied for second with 23 sacks allowed on the season. Quarterback Geno Smith has been sacked at least twice in the last seven games. Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is known for his relentless blitzing, and the Chiefs will get home two or more times.

picks.headline: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs
picks.blurb: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Kansas City Chiefs DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs with the football and looks to pass during the third quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs have beaten the New York Jets in four of their five meetings since 2011, with the most recent being a controversial 23-20 win in 2023. That game saw Michael Carter II's game-clinching interception negated by a phantom penalty on Sauce Gardner and wasted one of the best performances of Zach Wilson's career. In this matchup, the Chiefs will be heavy favorites despite having lost two in a row following a 5-0 start. Let's break down the Chiefs' roster going position by position: The Jets have Patrick Mahomes to reckon with this week, and he's having a solid season as he's posting a quarterback rating of 99.7; his best since 2022. Mahomes has 12 touchdowns and four interceptions and is coming off a good game against the Broncos where he passed for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. Behind Mahomes is a familiar face: Jets 2025 starter Justin Fields. Seventh round rookie Garrett Nussmeier is the number three. Offensive Line The Chiefs' interior line is the same as last year led by pro bowlers Creed Humphrey and Trey Smith at center and right guard respectively. Smith has a team-high five offensive penalties. Kingsley Suamataia completes the interior trio at left guard, although he's already been benched twice this year, including on Sunday where he was suddenly replaced before pre-game warmups by Mike Caliendo. That fuelled rumors that was was being disciplined by the coaching staff but Andy Reid denied this. Caliendo, who also started four games last year, has struggled in pass protection. Suamataia is expected to be back in the starting lineup for Sunday's game. The tackle positions have seen some changes as last year's starting right tackle, Jawaan Taylor, was released in March and the starting left tackle – 2025 first round pick Josh Simmons – is on injured reserve. Jaylon Moore, who started a handful of games last year, is currently starting at right tackle, while the left tackle is undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson, who is one of five undrafted rookies on the roster. Moore has given up a team-high three sacks, but Benson – while yet to surrender a sack – has given up the most pressure on the team. Moore missed week seven's game, so former New York Giant Joshua Ezeudu started at right tackle in that one. The other backups are center Hunter Nourzad and another undrafted rookie; tackle Diego Pounds. Running Backs The Chiefs' big offseason acquisition on offense was the reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. The move has been a resounding success as he rushed for 100 yards in four of his first five games as the Chiefs started 5-0. Since then, he's averaged just three yards per carry, though. Even so, he's just 10 yards off the league lead with 770 rushing yards. He has also caught 22 passes. There are two rookies backing up Walker – fifth round pick Emmett Johnson and the undrafted Jaydn Ott. Ott hasn't played yet, though. The Chiefs also have a fullback – Ben VanSumeren – on the roster. However, they will also use defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga in short yardage situations. He has even carried the ball twice. Pass catchers The Chiefs' top pass catching option has once again been tight end Travis Kelce, who has 410 receiving yards to lead the team. The leading pass catcher among the wide receivers is the speedy Xavier Worthy, who has 27 catches, albeit that he's only averaging 8.5 yards per catch. Despite some injury concerns and legal issues, Rashee Rice is now back in the lineup for the Chiefs. He has 20 catches in five games this year. Tyquan Thornton was also starting at wide receiver, but he's now on injured reserve. The backups are Jalen Royals, Andrew Armstrong, Nikko Remigio and fifth round rookie Cyrus Allen. Royals has seen the most action from this group. At tight end, Noah Gray is a solid contributor who gets plenty of playing time. Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley round out this group. Defensive Line The Chiefs' defensive line is anchored by pro bowler Chris Jones, although he is having a down year statistically with just half a sack, one tackle for loss and three quarterback hits. He had 7.5, 12 and 25 last year. George Karlaftis, who had six sacks last year, has a team-high two sacks and also leads the team with 16 quarterback hits (just one less than the rest of the team combined) and six tackles for loss. Karlaftis also has a team-high with eight passes defensed. In fact, these all eight of these came in the last five games. Prior to that, he had 17 in his first 67 NFL games. Tonga is the other starter at defensive tackle with Felix Anudike-Uzomah the other starting defensive end. Kansas City has been operating a three-man rotation inside with first round rookie Peter Woods getting plenty of playing time. However, Woods has been ruled out with a neck injury so Bryson Eason may need to step up. Last year's second round pick Omarr Norman-Lott remains on the PUP list. The backups on the edge are second round rookie R Mason Thomas and Ashton Gillotte. Undrafted rookie Jack Pyburn is also on the roster. Nick Bolton remains in a full-time role with Drue Tranquill on the field most of the time. Last year, Bolton had 154 tackles and Tranquill added 103. They've been productive this year, too, with Bolton on 68 tackles and Tranquill on 53 tackles, including five tackles for loss. Jack Cochrane gets playing time in three-linebacker sets, while Jeffrey Bassa has seen limited action. Cooper McDonald has yet to play any defensive snaps, though. Defensive Backs The Chiefs suffered a loss a few weeks ago when their top cornerback L'Jairus Sneed was placed on injured reserve. Sneed was also the team's primary slot corner, so they've been using Christian Roland-Wallace in that role for the past few weeks. Nohl Williams and first round rookie Mansoor Delane are the current starters on the outside, although Kristian Fulton started in place of Delane on Sunday. Delane has a shoulder issue which is likely to limit him for the rest of the season but he was expected to return against the Jets. However, he has been ruled out, so Fulton will presumably start again. Melvin Smith and fourth round rookie Jadon Canady are also available to provide depth at cornerback. The starting safeties are Chamarri Conner, who had 117 tackles last season, and offseason signing Alohi Gilman. Jaden Hicks has also been getting playing time in three-safety sets. He also started the first three games with Conner out. Undrafted rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa has played five snaps so far this season. Special Teams Former pro bowl kicker Harrison Butker is having a rough year with six missed field goals already and Justin Tucker waiting in the wings on the practice squad in case he should falter again. Punter Matt Araiza is having his best year statistically in his third season with the Chiefs, though. Remigio is the team's return specialist, although Johnson ends up sharing the work on kickoff returns. Remigio, who is yet to achieve a 50-yard return as he is halfway through his third season, is officially listed as questionable. Bassa and Nwankpa are the team's most productive players in kick coverage this season, but last year they were led by McDonald and Cochrane. Canady and Nwankpa have been the primary gunners.

Wilson — who started his professional career as the No. 10 pick in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft — has been in the league's concussion protocol and missed all of New York's practice sessions ahead of the Jets' tilt against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. away.headline: Jets vs Chiefs: Garrett Wilson headlines Jets’ inactives
away.blurb: Garrett Wilson will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs today. Wilson is in the concussion protocol and will miss his first game this season. Wilson’s absence will be a problem for the Jets passing game in a game when they will need every weapon they can find. However, unlike past years, the Jets have some pretty good weapons even without Wilson, including rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq and young veteran Adonai Mitchell. Together with the return of Breece Hall to the lineup and the emergence of Braelon Allen as one of the best young backs in the game, the Jets should be able to compensate fairly well for the loss of Wilson. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Joseph Ossai has been a disatrous free agent signing for the Jets thus far. He has missed all but three games with various injuries, and when he has played, he hasn’t been very effective. Signed for three years and $36+ million in this past offseason, Ossai has been a costly mistake to date. Perhaps he will eventually prove otherwise if he can just get healthy. Another issue on the above list is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. He has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. Unlike Ossai, health hasn’t been the issue for Wright. He just hasn’t been good enough to crack the lineup. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

home.headline: Chiefs in the market for WR after Xavier Worthy injury: report
home.blurb: Keep an eye out for any news regarding the Chiefs adding an offensive weapon this week. The Kansas City Chiefs are rumored to be in conversations about trading for a wide receiver ahead of the NFL ‘s deadline on Tuesday. On Sunday after the team’s 35-12 win over the New York Jets, those discussions only increased after the Chiefs lost receiver Xavier Worthy towards the end of the game with a hamstring injury. It’s unknown how severe his injury is and if he’ll miss any time, but the possibility of his absence makes the Chiefs more motivated to shop for a receiver. CBS’s Tracy Wolfson said on Sunday’s broadcast that general manager Brett Veach told her before the game that the team was in the market for a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday, and now with Worthy’s injury, it’s expected for them to make a trade happen. “As we’ve been talking about the lack of deep threats for the Chiefs, and I spoke with GM Brett Veach before the game, he told me that as the trade deadline approaches, the focus continues to be at that wide receiver position,” Wolfson said. “There has been increased dialogue this week, and he found that some of the major franchise players they looked at are off the market, but they will continue to have conversations over the next 24 hours to see if they can get something done by the trade deadline.” A few names have been linked to the Chiefs as rumors continue circulating. Indianapolis Colts’ Josh Downs requested a trade, and he pops up as an option for KC. The Jacksonville Jaguars have been more hesitant to listen to trade offers for their receiver Brian Thomas Jr., but the Chiefs are rumored to be interested in him. Jauan Jennings may have told the San Francisco 49ers that he liked his new home with the Minnesota Vikings, but he’s only playing on a one-year deal—he could easily be traded before the deadline. In the meantime, the Chiefs will rely on Rashee Rice as their top wide receiver. Tight end Travis Kelce still leads the Chiefs with 410 receiving yards. home.headline: Report: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes avoids major elbow injury
home.blurb: "Patrick took a pretty good shot to the throwing arm today and came off the field in some pain. We checked him out right away and he told us his elbow was sore, but he was determined to get back out there," Reid said. "He returned, made some throws, and kept competing the way he always does. He's one of the toughest players I've ever coached, and he doesn't like missing snaps." Nov 09 (Field Level Media) - Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a major injury to his right elbow, according to a media report Sunday night. An MRI exam revealed an elbow strain or sprain but no significant damage, NFL Network reported. Mahomes will be monitored for pain and swelling over the next few days, leaving his status uncertain for next Sunday's game against the host Atlanta Falcons. Mahomes injured his throwing arm during Kansas City's 35-12 victory over the New York Jets. He completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns but said afterward that his arm did not feel right early in the second half. "From the stories you hear, whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can't throw," Mahomes said. "Once I threw the football, I knew it wasn't -- hopefully, I haven't done the test yet -- it wasn't ligament-type stuff, it was more muscle-type stuff." Mahomes was drilled by Jets rookie edge rusher David Bailey while raring back to fire a pass downfield with 1:33 left in the first half. He came off the field supporting his right elbow with his left arm and appeared to be in significant pain. Head coach Andy Reid said the Chiefs would follow all of the proper steps to confirm Mahomes is not hurt. If upcoming tests give the Chiefs pause, Reid said the plan will be to "prepare Justin (Fields)" to face the Falcons on Sunday. Fields did not attempt a pass Sunday but ran twice for minus-1 yard. Mahomes returned to start Week 1 after sustaining a season-ending left knee injury in 2025.

Through seven games, they've scored the second-fewest points (16.7/contest), plus they've allowed the ninth-most points (25.9/game). Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. The Lions have also listed running back Sione Vaki (ankle) and Jacob Saylors (neck) as questionable. Campbell has been ruled out due to a neck injury that he suffered in Week 8 and he currently remains hospitalized. Head coach Dan Campbell mentioned Friday that Campbell continues to improve. Safety Kerby Joseph (knee), center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback DJ Reed (hip) and edge rusher DJ Wonnum (concussion) have also all been ruled out. The Dolphins have three players listed on their injury report as they have listed running backs Jaylen Wright (quad) and Kaytron Allen (quad) and edge rusher Malik Herring (neck) as questionable. Fans can catch Sunday afternoon’s matchup between the Lions and Dolphins from Hard Rock Stadium at 1 p.m. ET on FOX in both teams’ home markets and select other locations across the country. Check local listings for games available in your area . The Detroit Lions are on the road Sunday afternoon as they travel to take on the Miami Dolphins in a Week 9 interconference matchup. Detroit enters Sunday’s game with a 5-2 record after defeating the Minnesota Vikings at home in Week 8. In their victory over the Vikings, Jahmyr Gibbs led the way for the Lions as he recorded 153 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown while Jared Goff added 176 passing yards, one passing touchdown and an interception. The Lions will try to grab another victory Sunday as they face off against a struggling Dolphins team on the road. Miami enters Sunday’s contest with a 1-6 record after losing at home to the New England Patriots in Week 8. Malik Willis led the way for the Dolphins as he ended the game with 211 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and an interception while Ollie Gordon II recorded 69 rushing yards. While both teams are looking to pick up a victory in Sunday afternoon’s matchup, each may be without multiple key players due to injuries. Lions Injury Report: Will Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jack Campbell Play? The Lions have eight players listed on their injury report, including wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and linebacker Jack Campbell. If St. Brown is sidelined, Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa could both be in line for increased roles. home.blurb: Earlier in the week, coach Dan Campbell suggested Mays might miss Wednesday and Thursday’s practices, so this isn’t a surprise, but it’s still unclear whether he can return on Friday. Campbell said the team is preparing to start Scruggs this week, but nothing is finalized. Wonnum is still in the NFL’s concussion protocol, and while he still has a chance to pass the protocols this week, his lack of return to practice suggests he is a bit further back than hoped. Reed said he was in a good spot in his post-game media availability last Sunday, so his absence from practice could mean his injury was worse than he realized or that the team is giving the veteran extra time to be ready. We’ll find out more on Friday. Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding a walkthrough rather than a full practice. Jaylen Wright does not practice The Dolphins' second-string running back missed practice with a quadriceps injury. While Wright's contributions on offense have been minimal this year, picking up just 41 yards on 22 carries, he has been strong as a kick returner, where he is averaging 27.6 yards per kick and has a long of 79 yards. Dolphins rookie guard Kadyn Proctor fully participated in Wednesday's practice but remains in the league's concussion protocol, according to head coach Jeff Hafley. "He is progressing in the protocol," Hafley said. Jarrett Kingston, an August waiver claim from the Houston Texans for Miami, started in Proctor's place last week. Good news from Detroit's Jack Campbell The Lions' All-Pro linebacker sustained an ugly injury against the Vikings after tackling tight end T.J. Hockenson. Caught in an awkward position, Campbell hit Hockenson and had his head compress back onto his neck. He fell to the turf and lay motionless before being carted off the field and taken to a hospital. Campbell released a statement on Wednesday, indicating that he is progressing well in his recovery from the injury ( via Pride of Detroit ) : My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger

picks.blurb: Saints vs. Browns Predictions: Will New Orleans Take Advantage of Cleveland's QB Change? The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson . Here are our staff predictions. Grant Chachere , Lead Writer: W 24-10 This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints. Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin . Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase. This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up. However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis . Saints 24 Browns 10 Doug Joubert , Publisher: L 28-17 The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing. This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend. The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game. These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no. The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going. This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept). I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win. I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too. And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it. The New Orleans Saints return off their bye week as 3.5-point home favorites to host the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 8. M y top Browns vs. Saints predictions and NFL picks lean on a well-rested Saints squad to capitalize on a reeling Cleveland defense, and a team turning to backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders. TOP PICK Browns vs Saints prediction today: Saints moneyline I recommend the New Orleans Saints moneyline up to 65% . This is the third consecutive road game for the Cleveland Browns , while the Saints are coming off their bye week. Cleveland has also dipped to 28th in EPA per play and 26th in offensive DVOA over the past four weeks, and the Browns will have backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders behind center. Sanders threw for just 6.5 yards per attempt with a 51.9% completion percentage across his three road starts in 2025, and he finished the season with the lowest EPA per play and second-lowest completion percentage over expected among qualified QBs. New Orleans is positioned to outscore Cleveland. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough has led the offense to an above-average 23.1 points per game, and New Orleans will also have key starters back on the field on both sides of the ball. Browns vs Saints combo The Browns are slipping defensively and are turning to a backup quarterback in Sanders this week, while the Saints are coming off their bye week. picks.blurb: Final Prediction for Saints-Browns Week 9 Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Final Prediction for Saints-Browns Week 9 Matchup Caleb Yaccarino · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After two weeks without New Orleans Saints football, we are finally back. The Saints are also making their return to New Orleans, which may honestly be bad news for this team. The Saints have been unable to win a game at home this year, and some of their worst performances happened in New Orleans. For a team that has always valued the impact of playing at home, this is a really bad situation to be in, especially given how vocal fans can be. It also doesn't help that the pressure on the coaching staff to perform is palpable. The Saints also made some really important changes before this game. The Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, and they cut some players, including kicker Daniel Carlson and RB Kendre Miller. Each move made sense, and it is the first time we have seen real consequences from Kellen Moore's coaching staff. As I mentioned, the pressure is on this team, so we might as well try new things. For their opponent, it is a winnable game. The Cleveland Browns have been surprisingly one of the best teams in the NFL this season. They have had to make some crazy comebacks to make it happen, but QB Deshaun Watson is having a resurgence in his career. The defense is also playing really well, with the pass rush and pass defense standing out. But Watson is likely going to be out for this game. As of now, Watson has missed practice all week and is questionable for Sunday, so Shedeur Sanders will likely start for Cleveland. Although Sanders has not played yet this year, the Saints shouldn't overlook what the young QB can do. He had ups and downs throughout his rookie year, and if he is on point when facing the Saints' defense, it can be difficult to stop. The real worry for New Orleans is the Browns' defense. They have had run defense issues, so if the Saints defy all odds and fix the run game, that could be a way to win this game, but the rest of the defense will cause issues for the Saints. Now on to the prediction. Even with Watson likely being out, it's extremely difficult for me to choose the Saints. I do think it's going to be a close game, just not a victory for New Orleans. They need to prove the changes actually mattered first before I can believe something will change. For the score, I have the Browns winning 30-28.

away.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
away.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9.
