away.headline: Cleveland Browns Practice Report for Wednesday November 4 Week 9
away.blurb: The Cleveland Browns wrapped up practice Wednesday at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus in Berea, and there are nine players on the injury report. Quarterback Deshaun Watson, who took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the Week 8 game against the Pittsburgh, entered the concussion protocol this week. He did not practice on Wednesday. The Browns had a total of four players who did not practice in the first official session of the week, while five other players were listed as limited participants. No one on the practice report was able to take part in a full session. Browns defensive tackle Maliek Collins (elbow) left the Week 8 game against the Steelers due to an elbow injury. He suffered the injury in the second quarter, and he was considered questionable to return. And, return he did, as Collins made his way back into the game in the third quarter. He finished with four total stops and a tackle for loss in Pittsburgh. Also on defense, cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (wrist, ankle) and defensive end Jared Verse (knee) were listed as limited participants. All three played Sunday, with Schwesinger leading the way with 10 total stops, including four solo tackles. Denzel Boston Listed as Limited Participant Rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston (calf), who has been playing through injury for the past couple of weeks, was limited due to that aforementioned calf. He hasn't missed any game time, and he had six receptions for 37 yards, while tying tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for the game high with 12 targets in Week 8. Rounding things out on offensive, rookie offensive tackle Austin Barber (calf) did not practice, while center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee) was a limited participant. His named has dotted the injury report for several weeks, but he has been able to fight through the nagging lower-body injury to play. Safety Justin Reid , who initially did not practice Thursday because of concussion-like symptoms, is expected to play Sunday. Running back CJ Donaldson will not be available because of ongoing issues related to a concussion and his shoulder. For the Browns, the biggest storyline continues to center on the quarterback position. Their regular starter, Deshaun Watson (concussion), is questionable to play Sunday. The only other player ruled out for the Browns is defensive tackle Maliek Collins (elbow). home.headline: Saints' Jordyn Tyson reportedly set to make NFL debut vs. Browns after hamstring injury
home.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson will make his NFL debut against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Tyson was selected with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but a hamstring injury landed him on injured reserve during training camp. The Saints need to activate the rookie from injured reserve by Saturday afternoon for him to be eligible to play on Sunday. New Orleans has a 2-5 record, but remains in contention in a relatively weak NFC South. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

home.blurb: Speaking to reporters Monday, Saints coach Kellen Moore said “we anticipate Erik being out for a little bit,” and will manage McCoy on a “week-to-week” basis. STAFF PHOTO BY DAVID GRUNFELD Saints center Erik McCoy will miss time with bicep injury, but avoided ‘long-term’ setback BY LUKE JOHNSON | Staff writer Luke Johnson Erik McCoy will once again be sidelined by an injury , but it appears the veteran New Orleans Saints center avoided the worst possible outcome. McCoy exited the Saints’ 23-22 win against the Cleveland Browns in the fourth quarter with an injured bicep. Backup William Sherman handled all the snaps for both the go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter and the eventual game-winning touchdown drive in overtime. Considering that McCoy missed the final 10 weeks of last season with a torn left bicep, the news that he will not require a long-term absence was positive. Moore was unable to say whether McCoy injured the same bicep that he did a year ago. When he has been on the field, McCoy has performed like one of the NFL’s better centers. The 2019 second-rounder made Pro Bowls after the 2023 and 2024 seasons. But injuries have piled up in recent years. McCoy played in just seven games each of the last two seasons, and suffered this new bicep injury in the eighth game of the Saints’ 2026 season. New Orleans has a couple options to replace McCoy in the starting lineup. More than likely, the Saints will follow the same script they did in Sunday’s win and play William Sherman in McCoy’s place. But the Saints could also pivot and shift Cesar Ruiz inside to center, allowing 2026 fourth-rounder Jeremiah Wright to play at right guard. Ruiz played center at the University of Michigan and handled a few snaps during training camp. Faced with a similar choice last season, the Saints opted to keep Ruiz at guard and insert Luke Fortner into the lineup at center, with the rationale being that they did not want a downgrade at two positions. Flash forward heading into Week 9, and it couldn't be more opposite with the Giants as the front-runner to win the NFC East for the first time in 15 years, last doing so when the franchise won its fourth Super Bowl in 2011. Art Stapleton The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 23 Here's why: John Harbaugh's team had a great bye week, with Dallas' stunning overtime defeat to Arizona increasing Big Blue's lead in the NFC East without even playing. QB J.J. McCarthy was outstanding in his first start against the Texans, clicking downfield with WR Malik Nabers, who had his fourth straight 100-yard receiving game. The Giants have not won in Philadelphia since Tom Coughlin was head coach in 2013, and they have not scored an offensive TD there in a win since their Super Bowl season of 2011. It's time for the streak to end. Bert Bainbridge The pick: Giants 30, Eagles 17 Here's why: No one thought this would be the reality at the midway point of the season with the Giants in the driver seat in the NFC East and the Eagles in free fall mode. Fresh off a bye, the G-Men go into Philadelphia and defeat the Birds at Lincoln Financial Field for the first time in 13 years. The pick: Giants 27, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are spiraling as the key injuries continue to mount, especially on offense. The Giants are the better team right now, and are fresh off of a bye week. Expect Big Blue to earn a relatively comfortable win. The pick: Giants 34, Eagles 20 Here's why: The Eagles are a mess right now and that's a big reason why the Giants are in prime position to win the NFC East. The pick: Giants 23, Eagles 16 Here's why: The Eagles are going nowhere this season, and with the Cowboys and Commanders not showing to be real threats in the NFC East at this point, John Harbaugh and the Giants are seizing the opportunity. picks.headline: Why the Giants Will Beat the Eagles, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Eagles, Why They Won't, and a Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Why the Giants Will Beat the Eagles, Why They Won't, and a Prediction New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh brings a 15-3 record in games played following the bye. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Patricia Traina · New York Giants On SI Sun, November 8, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants are rolling with a winning record, a relatively healthy roster, and all the reasons in the world to show up Sunday in Philadelphia, where they haven't won in 13 seasons, and dominate a bruised, battered and broken Eagles team that has, for the most part, had their number. But head coach John Harbaugh's message to his players is not to let the rivalry's bitterness get in the way or close their eyes to the need to take care of business. "It's just a really important game for our team. Really, honestly, that's really what overwhelms your thinking, the opportunity that we have against a big rival," he said. "We know what kind of environment it's going to be. We know what type of game it's going to be. We understand all that. And that's what you get ready for." The Giants, who roll into Philadelphia as 3-point favorites according to FanDuel Sportsbook , also understand that, rivalries and hard feelings aside, this game is a chance to build on their lead atop the NFC East. "We're trying to win the division first. That's our first goal here. This game will go a long way toward that. That's why it's so important," Harbaugh said. "Division games are big. Division games on the road are really big. Those are big wins if you can get them. They're tough to get. It's a big challenge. We're excited about the opportunity, but we understand it's a daunting challenge." Why the Giants Will Beat the Eagles The Giants have done a tremendous job this season of dominating time of possession on offense. New York ranks second (behind the Bears) in average time of possession at 32:30. The Eagles, meanwhile, rank 28th (tied with Dallas) at 28:24. A big reason for the Eagles' struggle to control the game tempo is drive sustainability. They are tied with the Baltimore Ravens for the most three-and-out drives in the league (35). The Giants are tied with the Patriots and Lions for the sixth-fewest (19). Simply put, if the Giants can keep controlling the clock as they have through their first seven games, they stand a more than decent chance of snapping the 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia. A key will be running the ball against the league's 28th-ranked run defense (131.9 rushing yards per game). It's not the best week for the Giants to potentially be without Cam Skattebo, their top running back, who is listed as doubtful on the team's injury report. Still, the hope is that Devin Singletary, expected to be the RB1 this week if Skattebo is inactive, and the rest of the running game can rise to the occasion. Why the Giants Won't Beat the Eagles Ever notice how something screwy always seems to happen to the Giants when they go to Lincoln Financial Field? Skattebo's ankle injury, Victor Cruz's knee injury, the 2022 divisional playoff blowout loss, the 2014 shutout, the first the Giants had suffered since 1996... the list goes on and on. But seriously, the only way the Giants conceivably lose to the Eagles is if they beat themselves with sloppy play, stupid penalties, missed tackles and other errors that tip the scales in the Eagles' favor. That includes turnovers. The Eagles have four takeaways all season, tied for last with the Colts. The Giants, who have 11 giveaways (tied for seventh), will undoubtedly want to make sure that total doesn't increase. Tactically, it may come down to the Eagles' rushing attack versus the Giants' run defense. Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is playing despite hamstring and back injuries, and head coach Nick Sirianni has decided to change things at quarterback by benching Tanner McKee for the more mobile Joe Milton III. The Giants have struggled this season against mobile quarterbacks, and their run defense has allowed 4.8 yards per carry overall. If New York doesn't shut down the run, regardless of who carries the ball, it could make for a long afternoon. The New York Giants are in a strong position to win their first game against the Eagles in Philadelphia in 13 seasons. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Harbaugh might not be interested in what has transpired between these two teams in the past, but he does own a 15-3 record in games played after the bye, so he knows how to get his team ready coming out of a break. Both teams are banged up, but the Giants' depth has clearly been much better than the Eagles'. There are too many signs pointing to the Giants finally ending their 13-year drought in the City of Brotherly Love in what would be a huge morale-boosting win and would further extend their lead over the rest of the NFC East. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy exited the team's Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles after taking a massive hit from linebacker Zack Baun. He eventually returned to the game after a trip to the locker room, but the team has since revealed if it could affect his playing status moving forward. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , McCarthy suffered a hip pointer and the team is confident that he will be ready for Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. That is certainly good news, given how the injury initially looked. He was in visible pain on the sideline before heading to the locker room and being replaced by backup quarterback Jameis Winston. The Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy following starter Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in September. New York then switched to McCarthy as its starter ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, and he has played quite well since, throwing for 622 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

Skattebo hurt his hamstring during overtime of the Giants’ thrilling pre-bye week win in Houston. He downplayed the injury after the game. With Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve and out for at least the next four games, the Giants on Sunday might need to turn to Devin Singletary as their primary back. Carter was not on the injury report at all leading up to the Houston game. But a game prior, he was listed as questionable to face the Saints because of a calf issue. picks.headline: Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13
picks.blurb: Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Myles Garrett picks up 3.0 sacks in return, Rams beat Commanders 20-13 LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Myles Garrett #95 celebrates with Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams after sack against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) (Getty Images) Myles Simmons · ProFootball Talk on NBC Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 9:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome back, Myles Garrett. The star edge rusher returned from a knee procedure and showed the difference he can make, racking up 3.0 sacks in the Rams' 20-13 victory over the Commanders on Sunday afternoon. Garrett's first sack also forced a fumble, as he poked the ball out from quarterback Jayden Daniels in the second quarter. That led to a field goal late in the half, which cut Washington's lead to 10-6 at halftime. Garrett then had two more in the fourth quarter, one of which came after he'd just been flagged for an offside penalty. While Garrett starred on defense, receiver Puka Nacua paced the offense with 14 catches for 150 yards with a touchdown. His 14 receptions are the third-most he's had in a single game in his career. He also had a pair of carries for 20 yards. The Commanders had a 10-6 lead at halftime from a 37-yard field goal and a 7-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels to Van Jefferson. The Rams got two field goals from Brandon McManus for their six points. But the Rams were able to double up with a touchdown on their first drive of the second half. Blake Corum ran it in for a 1-yard score to cap an eight-play, 69-yard drive. And while a Matthew Stafford interception allowed the Commanders to tie the game at 13-13, Stanford then threw a touchdown to Nacua to put the Rams ahead for good. Washington had a chance to at least tie the game late, but time ran out on their last drive. Daniels finished the game 24-of-35 for 273 yards with a touchdown. He had four carries for 16 yards. Stafford finished 26-of-43 for 228 yards with a TD and a pick. At 5-4, the Rams are now above .500 for the first time this season and on a three-game winning streak. The team will be on the road to face division-rival Arizona next weekend before a Week 11 bye. The Commanders have fallen to 2-5-1. They won't have much time to think about their missed opportunities, as they'll face the Giants on Thursday night in Week 10.

He has concerns about the receiver’s longevity given his injury history. “If you think about how much he’s been hurt, and he’s been hurt because of his physicality in play. He’s not afraid to go across the middle, he seeks contact after he catches the football, he takes shots in games where you like, damn, is he even gonna get up from those shots? So I think more than anything right now with the Rams, because this is going to be your number one receiver. Davante was playing great, but Davante was brought in to complement Puka Nacua based on all of the things that he did in this offense,” Spears said. away.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett’s huge injury return is a Los Angeles first since Aaron Donald
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett made an immediate impact in his return, notching three sacks and forcing a fumble during Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The performance put the 30-year-old in rare company, as he became the first player in franchise history to record three sacks and a forced fumble since star pass rusher Aaron Donald accomplished the feat back in 2020. His first sack came in the second quarter when he knocked the ball out of quarterback Jayden Daniels’ hands. Linebacker Omar Speights recovered the fumble, helping Los Angeles get into position for a field goal that reduced Washington’s advantage to 10-6 before halftime. Garrett added two more sacks in the fourth quarter, including one against Daniels after coming around left tackle Brandon Coleman. His final takedown turned out to be a game-changer, as he beat the replacement center with a quick move through the middle to prevent the Commanders from building momentum during their late comeback attempt. Garrett’s return helped Los Angeles improve to 5-4, extend its winning streak to three games and move above .500 for the first time this season. The Rams will next face the division-rival Arizona Cardinals before entering its Week 11 bye. Garrett, who underwent knee surgery in mid-September after initially attempting to play through the injury, missed seven weeks before returning to action in Week 9. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year wasted little time demonstrating his value, generating six quarterback pressures on 27 pass-rush attempts, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He also managed a 22.2% pressure rate while playing 35 of the Rams’ 58 defensive snaps. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The three-sack performance was Garrett’s ninth career game with at least three sacks, the most by any player since Hall of Famer DeMarcus Ware in 2014, according to ESPN Research. He also brought his career sack total to 128.5, tying Hall of Famer Jared Allen for the second-most sacks by a player through his first 10 NFL seasons since the statistic became official in 1982. The contest also was the first time Garrett shared the field with Donald , who retired in March 2024. Across 23 plays with both defensive stars on the field, the Rams surrendered just 5.0 yards per play and recorded four sacks. During the other 19 plays, the defense allowed 8.0 yards per play and a touchdown without producing a sack. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested
away.blurb: The Broncos play the Carolina Panthers in Week 9, and it's the team's final game before the Week 10 bye, which comes at a perfect time. The team's final injury report does test the depth of this defense but also sees the return of a key rotational player on offense. All of Dondrea Tillman, Talanoa Hufanga, Kris Abrams-Draine, Brandon Jones, and Eyioma Uwazurike are either out or questionable in Week 9: Even with Bryant being listed as questionable, he'll play in Week 9: Hufanga's return will be the key to watch, and if you look at Denver's injury report from Week 8, there seems to be a good chance that the starting safety returns: In this practice week, Hufanga went DNP, Limited, and Limited and is listed as questionable. Just last week, the Broncos saw both Zach Allen and Jaylen Waddle have the exact same practice week, and both were also listed as questionable. Both played, so there is reason to believe that the Broncos took Hufanga's practice statuses this week with the same idea in mind. It does flat-out stink that the Broncos are going to still be down a starting safety with a likely Hufanga return. Jones hurt his hamstring during the win over Kansas City in Week 8 and did not practice all week. This article was originally published on predominantlyorange.com as Broncos final injury report: Pat Bryant's return, depth on defense tested . For the most part, the Denver Broncos have stayed healthy this year, but they have dealt with a good bit of injuries to primary depth, rotational players. We have already seen Jonah Coleman spent time on IR. Tyler Badie and RJ Harvey are both on IR, along with Jonah Elliss. The team has also seen Pat Bryant be placed on IR. Patrick Surtain II just recently missed time as well. All in all, Denver is certainly no strangers to injuries this year, but, for the most part, the primary starters are healthy and in a good spot. Denver Broncos final injury report for Week 9 against the Panthers In an ideal world, both Tillman and Hufanga suit up. If not, the depth of this defense is going to be tested big-time. The offense is clearly much healthier, as every one of the primary starters are healthy enough to play. I guess if we had to 'pick' one side to be hurt more, it would be the defense given how good this unit has been for years now, but that doesn't make this week's report any less shaky. The Broncos getting a win in Week 9. moving to 7-2, and having two weeks off would be the absolute best-case scenario. Denver's bye would allow every banged-up player to get healthier, and it would also present a perfect opportunity for the team to add a player or two at the NFL Trade Deadline and get them up to speed with the bye. Even in a loss, the Broncos sitting at 6-3 would still position themselves well down the stretch, especially with the ease of the remaining schedule. Houston looks to keep Los Angeles winless, and my Texans vs. Chargers prediction says the Texans have the edge on both sides of the ball as 5.5-point road favorites. The Chargers own the league's worst scoring offense at 14.1 points per game, and they'll face a Houston pass rush that keeps getting home. Check out my NFL picks for Sunday, Nov. 8, plus our Week 9 best bets for every game, with kickoff set for 4:05 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium on CBS. TOP PICK Texans vs Chargers prediction: Texans -5.5 Play up to 57%. The Houston Texans may be sitting at 2-5, but they're a much better offensive team. Houston is averaging 23.6 ppg (12th) compared to a league-worst 14.1 points per contest for the Los Angeles Chargers , one of the games in our Week 9 against-the-spread picks . I also expect a long day for Justin Herbert , who has already been sacked 23 times. He's up against a Texans pass rush that has the fifth-most sacks in the AFC . Will Anderson Jr. leads the unit with 7.5 sacks. C.J. Stroud , meanwhile, has thrown just one interception this season. Houston has also won both road games this season, and I expect the Texans to cover on Sunday. Texans vs Chargers combo I expect a low-scoring Week 9 affair. Herbert will likely struggle to move the ball, given Houston's success pressuring the quarterback, and LA hasn't scored a touchdown in back-to-back games . Houston has been more productive offensively, but the Texans haven't been particularly consistent either. I expect them to score 20-25 points while limiting the Chargers to 10-14, keeping this contest comfortably Under 40.5 (see our Week 9 Over/Under predictions for every game). Tre' Harris has been one of LA's more reliable targets this season. He has 18 receptions on 29 targets, and the youngster has cashed the Over in three of his last four outings . Houston's secondary isn't great, ranking 28th in passing yards allowed. Tre' Harris Over 2.5 receptions Texans vs Chargers touchdown scorer: Nico Collins Play up to 42%. Nico Collins is second on the Texans in receptions (24) and tied for first in TDs (3). He has five red-zone targets this season with three catches, turning two of those into scores . Stroud frequently targets him, and Collins' physicality is a major strength near the goal line. Even though the Chargers have been particularly solid at defending in the red zone, Collins is my strongest look among Week 9 anytime touchdown picks on Sunday. Texans vs Chargers player prop: Woody Marks 60+ rushing yards With David Montgomery still injured, Woody Marks will be RB1 once again today, and I expect him to flourish. Even though the Texans don't run the football a whole lot, they could resort to putting the ball in Marks' hands more. L.A. is stingy against the pass, but they're 23rd against the run , allowing 124.6 yards per game on the ground. Marks has logged at least 15 carries in each game since Montgomery was injured, and he's cleared this total in two of those games . In the other, he still finished with 56 yards, just a tad below the threshold. He'll be a force at SoFi, making him a strong target among Week 9 player props . Want more NFL player props? The Chargers have lost their first seven games and are the only winless team left in the league. However, the Chargers can turn things around with a win against the struggling Texans, who are coming off of their bye week. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , the Chargers are an underdog by 5.5 points. Let's take a look at some predictions for the game. Over/Under: 40.5 The Chargers have not scored an offensive touchdown in nearly 30 possessions. Meanwhile, the Texans have one of the best defenses on paper in the league. They haven't performed up to their standard this season, but they remain a big threat on defense. On offense, the Texans have been up and down over the last couple of games, but given how the Chargers have performed recently, this has the feel of a low-scoring affair. Playing at home against the Texans does provide a chance for them to beat this streak, but the Texans are coming into this game hungry and desperate, given that they still have playoff hopes alive, even if they are faint. The Texans should be a little healthier coming off of their bye, and that should give them a chance to come in and beat the Chargers. Prediction: Texans -5.5 Until the Chargers prove they can do something on offense, it's hard for me to say they can win many football games. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Texans: 4 bold predictions for Week 9 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Chargers vs. Texans: 4 bold predictions for Week 9 matchup Ricardo Sandoval , Chargers Wire · Chargers Wire Sun, November 8, 2026 at 2:22 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chargers will do all they can to win their first game of the 2026 season. Los Angeles remains the only winless team in the NFL. They are certainly one of the league's more disappointing teams, and the Texans are in the same boat. The Chargers (0-7) will host the Texans (2-5) this Sunday. The two teams are nowhere near where they expected to be, but they'll hope this week helps one of them turn the tide. Here are four bold predictions for Week 9. J ustin Herbert throws for 300+ yards and one touchdown Herbert is coming off a season-high 257 passing yards. The 28-year-old completed 24 of 32 passes, another season-high. Although he recorded two interceptions, Herbert showed clear signs of improvement. Houston's defense allows 244 passing yards per game, the fifth-most in the NFL, which helps Herbert build on his Week 8 performance. Chargers force C.J. Stroud into two t urnovers The Chargers' defense is far and away their best unit of the three. I expect them to wreak some havoc on Stroud, although he has taken exceptional care of the football. Stroud has 11 touchdowns to just one interception and no fumbles. However, I'm predicting the Texans quarterback has at least one interception and a forced fumble. Chargers running backs combine for 100+ rushing yards The Chargers offense hasn't rushed for 75+ in their last two games. Los Angeles rushed for 64 yards against the Rams, averaging 2.6 yards per carry. Omarion Hampton could see an increased role in the backfield, with a fierce pass rush led by Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter. The Texans' rush defense is allowing 3.8 yards per carry (9th) and 98.0 yards per game (11th). While the Chargers' rush offense hasn't been what we expected, I think they'll find a better groove in Week 9, despite their opponent. Chargers score two touchdowns After going 27 consecutive offensive drives without scoring a touchdown, the Chargers will get in the end zone, not once, but twice. One of those touchdowns will come through the air, while the other will be on the ground. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

Now, after continuing to get back to 100% from said groin issue, it seems like he's all set to play on Sunday. As for Pitre, his return to the lineup is due for a bit more attention. Pitre has been sidelined for the Texans since suffering an AC joint sprain in his shoulder against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. David Montgomery Remains Out for Sunday Head coach DeMeco Ryans made it clear on Wednesday that David Montgomery will be missing his third-straight game this weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers. And on Thursday, he logged his second DNP of the week . Another starter who's been missing time for the Texans–– but on the defensive side of the ball–– is safety Reed Blankenship, who's missed his fifth-straight practice as a DNP, and is trending towards being out against Los Angeles for Week 9 . If Blankenship was just dealing with concussion protocol, there's a chance that if he is able to practice in limited capacity on Friday and clear protocol within 24 hours. But Blankenship is also dealing with a hand issue that might be making his return to play more complicated. home.headline: Justin Herbert injury: How does Chargers QB’s setback impact NFL trade deadline?
home.blurb: Justin Herbert suffered a finger injury , playing through the injury for a few plays, eventually moving to the blue medical tent once the offense was off the field. Once it was time for the offense to go back on the field, Herbert stayed back and found himself on the bench watching backup QB DJ Uiagalelei finish out the blowout loss at the hands of the Houston Texans. Of course, only time will tell, but it was only logical when the team was 0-5; it is even more logical with the team being 0-8 and with an injured QB. To go full fire-sale mode, some names to look out for on the trade market: The Los Angeles Chargers have fallen to 0-8, already finding themselves in what we all thought was the worst possible situation for the franchise after their semi-successful 2024 and 2025 seasons. Unfortunately, in classic Chargers fashion, it got worse . While information has yet to be finalized on the exact injury Herbert has suffered, it seems that the consensus is a broken middle finger on his non-throwing hand. Herbert has played through broken fingers before, but it seems that the team may need time to consider if he should continue to play and risk more injury. Now, with this hesitancy, this could very well change the Bolts' outlook on the NFL trade deadline, which is right around the corner, being marked as Nov. 10, 2026. Does Justin Herbert's Injury Finally Allow the Chargers to Trade Away Players? With the Bolts being 0-8, NFL teams were rightfully calling Los Angeles to ask about some of the team's players in hopes of hoping their own roster. The Chargers should be answering those calls and looking to build for their future, not for the 0-8 2026 Chargers. Unfortunately, Joe Hortiz has seemingly been unwilling to move away from players, with reporters saying the Chargers "still have belief" prior to this Texans loss. Now, with another loss and their star QB injured, can they finally turn the other way and sell off assets? Khalil Mack: The most spoken-about trade asset . He has mentioned he does not want to be traded, but it is worth mentioning that the veteran EDGE has plenty of value to other teams...if Mack were to change his mind. Donte Jackson: Another veteran who could have some value for a team in need of a starting-caliber DB. Even with the Chargers having injuries piling up at the position, it could be smart to let young practice squad players play rather than letting Jackson play for no team-related upside. Dalvin Tomlinson: One of the team's better run defenders could find his way on the market, as he is playing well, is healthy and is 32 years old. The Chargers have other options in Jamaree Caldwell and Nick Barrett who could take some snaps as the position. Daiyan Henley: A young LB who had a 2024 season filled with promise. He had an interception against the Houston Texans, but he is obviously in need of a fresh start. He could possibly be valued highly around the league considering his age and history of strong play. home.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
home.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

It’s not who you play but when you play them. The Green Bay Packers will face the New England Patriots on Sunday. It’s a measuring-stick game for the Packers, who believe they are Super Bowl contenders. The Patriots played in the Super Bowl last year and believe they have the goods to take the next step. With a top-tier quarterback and coach and a strong defense, they will be a formidable challenge. The Patriots, however, will play without their top two receivers, A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Their premier tight end, Hunter Henry, is questionable with a foot injury that held him out of practice to start the week. Their starting guards, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu, are on injured reserve. So is their top pass rusher, Harold Landry. Can the Packers take advantage of the “when you play them” part of that adage? Here are our weekly game predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Patriots Prediction The Packers have had some good fortune this season. They faced the Buccaneers without Baker Mayfield and the Bears without Caleb Williams. They will have more good fortune against the Patriots. While Drake Maye, last year’s MVP runner-up, will be the starting quarterback, he’s going to be playing with an incredibly shorthanded group of receivers. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams are not the same as A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Good quarterbacks can make it work with whoever, so this won’t be a layup victory for Jonathan Gannon’s defense. However, New England’s pass protection has been leaky, with Maye facing the fourth-highest pressure rate in the league. Can the Patriots’ receivers get open before the Packers’ pass rush arrives on the scene? Added together, the game has been put on a silver platter for Green Bay’s defense to be the most powerful unit on the field. On the other side of the ball, it’s going to be a challenging day for Jordan Love, as well. The Packers, of course, can’t run the football, and it’s having an impact on the passing game with the play-action attack having become irrelevant . If the Packers can’t run the ball – and what reason is there to believe they will? – they’re going to have to deal with the teeth of the Patriots’ strong pass rush, which ranks fifth in sack percentage. Elijah Ponder – the best pass rusher that nobody has ever heard of – is seventh in the league with six sacks. With 3.5 sacks, Christian Barmore powers the interior rush. “He’s a really good player,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said of Ponder, an undrafted free agent last year. “To be truthful, I hadn’t heard a whole lot about him until I started watching the tape and I’m like who is this guy? What’s his story? How do we not know about him? Everybody knows about him now. When you look at their edges, all three of those guys that are really doing the bulk of the work are really good players, and you couple that with the interior guys, it’s a really formidable front.” That could mean limited time for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to beat the premier cornerback duo of Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. “Really good DBs,” Love said. “I think they do a lot of things very well. I think as anything, it’s a challenge for me, for the receivers on the outside to be able to go see how good we can be and how good we can attack them and make plays against them. I think they do a really good job. I think Gonzalez is definitely one of the best in the league and he makes plays. I feel like for us, it’s a fun test.” Ultimately, I’m taking the Packers, who are 3-point underdogs at FanDuel Sportsbook . Both quarterbacks are really good, but I’ll take Watson and Golden vs. Gonzalez and Davis over Hollins and Douglas vs. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse. In a close game, the Packers will fail to run out the clock but the defense will save the day. And they’ll need it, with the Bears and Lions favored to win their games against the Buccaneers and Dolphins, respectively, while the first-place Vikings are underdogs against Buffalo. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 20. Bill’s Record: 6-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Patriots Prediction Everything outside of the field favors New England in this game with the return of Rob Gronkowski and Tom Brady, which has been discussed all week. The reality on the field, however, is that the Packers have more healthy players than the Patriots do. The Patriots are missing their top two receivers and their starting tight end is going to be hobbled, at minimum, if he can play. Drake Maye and Jordon Love are both being asked to carry a heavy load, but Love has a better supporting cast around him. In addition, Jonathan Gannon should be able to create enough confusion for Maye to make a couple of mistakes that swing the game in the Packers’ favor. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 24, Patriots 17. Jacob’s Record: 5-3. So do the New England Patriots, who lost in last year’s Super Bowl. On Sunday, these storied teams will collide in Foxborough in what is truly a measuring-stick game for the Packers. The Patriots are three-point favorites. With Tom Brady on the call and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame, here are three reasons why the Packers will spoil the party and earn a statement win. 1. Depleted Patriots Offense The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year despite the lack of a legit threat at receiver. So, they attempted to rectify that problem by signing Romeo Doubs, who had a solid four seasons with the Packers, and trading for A.J. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowler who had surpassed 1,000 yards in six of his first seven seasons. Neither player will be on the field for this game, though. Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and Brown is out again with a knee injury. Combined with the questionable status of top tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, the Packers’ strong defense will face a diluted New England attack. Without Brown and Doubs and with Henry limited to eight snaps with an injured foot, the Patriots needed to rally past the lowly Dolphins last week. The Patriots were held to merely 313 yards. The key for the Packers will be limiting the Rhamondre Stevenson-led running game and putting the pressure on New England’s passing game to make plays against a Packers defense that ranks fourth in opponent passer rating. “I think first of all, he’s an elite quarterback in the pocket, out of the pocket,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said of Drake Maye. “He’s extremely dangerous. He can make any throw. Obviously, he’s super-smart. “They got a great offensive coordinator, great receivers, great playmakers around him and, obviously, when the run game’s going they can do everything and they can throw it just as good as they can run it. So, we’re going to have our hands full for sure and got to make sure that we’re ready to play.” Prediction: The Patriots are going to have a hard time stringing together sustained success on offense. 2. Drake Maye May Screw Up Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is one of the best in the business. He was one vote away from winning NFL MVP last year. However, unless you’re one of the undisputed elite quarterbacks, a quarterback oftentimes is only as good as his supporting cast. So, while Maye is seventh in completion percentage, third in yards per attempt and fifth in touchdowns, only three quarterbacks have thrown more than Maye’s eight interceptions and his six fumbles are one off the unwelcome NFL lead. “I think speaking from playing zone coverage, they’ve got great eyes,” Maye told reporters this week. “They got eyes on the quarterback, they make plays on the football. They can, obviously, catch well. The safeties are great players. They do a lot of things well and they read the quarterback very well, mix up in zone looks. Tip balls have turned into picks that they’ve shown. “So, they’ve just had a habit of creating turnovers in the pocket with the quarterback. They have got some free rushers’ help, too, of the quarterback panicking and trying to fit some stuff to tight windows. They’re good at keeping you in some negative plays. They make you go longer distances. It’s hard.” In the Patriots’ three losses, Maye has thrown three touchdowns vs. six interceptions. In the five wins, it’s 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. His eight interceptions equal last year’s total (in less than half the attempts) are only two off his total from his rookie season in 2024. Prediction: It only takes one big mistake to swing a game between equal teams. Based on this season, Maye is more apt to make that mistake. 3. Turnovers (And Taking Advantage of Them) “The ball” is the most important thing in the sport, coach Matt LaFleur likes to say. Teams that take away and protect the ball tend to win; teams that don’t tend to lose. The Packers are tied for fourth in the league at plus-4 in turnovers. After creating only 14 takeaways last season – when Micah Parsons was on the field for 14 games – they rank second in the league with 15 takeaways this season. The Patriots this year are minus-7 overall; only the white-flag-of-surrender-waving Colts are worse at minus-11. Their 15 giveaways are the third-most in the league. Added together, you get this chart. Points Off Turnovers through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/UmVq9xw7uU The Packers are third in the league by scoring 52 points off takeaways; the Patriots are tied for 23rd with 20 points off takeaways. Green Bay’s aggressive, playmaking defense works hand-in-hand with quarterback Jordan Love’s aggressive, playmaking approach to the position. “Nobody’s had more 20-yard pass plays,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. “(Love is) a quarterback that’s wildly efficient. He has a few off-days, but they’re few and far between. They throw shots. They’ve, obviously, great speed on the edges. They have an excellent tight end, Tucker Kraft, and now getting [Josh] Jacobs back, it seems like they’re trying to work him back in there a little bit more and see what he can do for them in the red zone and things like that. I think they’ve protected better the last few games. “I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that’s an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he’s able to find [Matthew] Golden, [Christian] Watson or Tucker Kraft. Defensively, very physical. They have the second-most negative plays and created the second-most negative plays in the league. Seventeen percent of their drives end in a turnover, so that leads the league, as well.” Love is cooking. He and Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with at least two touchdown passes in seven games this season. “Our goal every week is to go 1-0, and this is a very good team,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, they were in the Super Bowl last year for a reason. They’re very good in, really, all three phases. They got an elite defense. I think they do a lot of things really well. They got two really good corners on the outside. “Yeah, I got a lot of respect for them. It’s always a good test, but I think the goal for us to see how we can go out there and execute the plan, and the goal is to come away victorious. We know to put ourselves in the best position late in the season. We got to really just win every game, and that’s the mindset of going 1-0 every week. It’ll be a good test for us.” Prediction: The Packers have at least two takeaways in five consecutive games. If they can do it again, they’ll win. LaFleur has covered 65.1% of all games when his team is catching points, and I believe this is another very good spot for Green Bay to potentially steal a victory. The narrative surrounding the Packers offense has to do with their lack of pass protection, as every mention of their future outlook as a Super Bowl contender is usually followed by a comment regarding their offensive line issues. Jordan Love is navigating those issues quite well, as it may be surprising to some that he has just a 32% pressure rate on all of his dropbacks. Only seven quarterbacks with 200 or more dropbacks have faced pressure less often than Love this season. We already know Green Bay struggles to run the football effectively, and that data point is completely baked into the line here. Sure, most of the offensive success for this team is squarely on the shoulders of Love, but that is something I am completely comfortable with against a Patriots team that ranks 26th in quick pressure percentage. Quick pressures occur within 2.5 seconds of the snap, and it is not something I am concerned about happening regularly in this matchup. If there is a signal caller who will be under constant duress in this game, it is likely to be Drake Maye . Maye has regained his MVP-level play from a season ago, but protection issues that plagued this team in the playoffs remain. The 44% pressure rate allowed by the New England offensive line is the highest rate league-wide. The Packers are generating pressure at the 12th-highest rate, but more importantly, they are converting those pressures into sacks. Green Bay has 22 sacks on the season, the sixth-most in the NFL. While the Packers' pass rush is undoubtedly above average, it has been the coverage in the secondary that has been this defense's biggest strength. Green Bay allows just 6.2 yards per pass attempt (fifth-best) while also ranking among the top five pass defenses in expected points added (EPA) per pass against. During Maye's hot streak, he has been doing his best work when throwing down the field. Maye leads the league in touchdown passes of 20 or more yards downfield this season, in addition to being efficient in the intermediate areas of the field. Over the past five weeks, Maye has completed 67% of his throws that have traveled more than 10 yards past the line of scrimmage. However, it is worth noting he has not played the most difficult slate of defenses during that stretch. The Packers are a completely different animal defensively than the teams Maye has shredded in recent weeks. During that same span of five games, Green Bay is second in the league in defensive EPA. The Packers specialize in limiting explosive plays — allowing the third-fewest of any defense in football. On throws 10 or more yards downfield, the Packers have allowed opposing quarterbacks to complete just 44% of their passes, generating seven interceptions while allowing just two touchdowns. The Patriots are not equipped to pressure Love as often as they need to, but the Packers do possess the tools to halt numerous New England possessions with their sticky coverage and timely pass rush led by Devonte Wyatt and Lukas Van Ness . Packers vs Patriots Spread Prediction, Betting Analysis Jordan Love and Drake Maye are in good form — both rank inside the top 12 of qualifying quarterbacks in adjusted net yards per attempt, have passer ratings that exceed 105.0 when kept clean and boast identical big-time throw rates. Let's call it a wash at quarterback. The team protecting their passer more cleanly also happens to be the team with the decided advantage defensively. Getting three points with the Packers in this spot is a tremendous value. Add in Matt LaFleur's success rate at covering the number as an underdog during his tenure as Packers head coach, and this may be one of my strongest positions of the NFL season thus far. It feels like they're coming off a bye heading into Week 9's matchup with the New England Patriots. And to be fair, it was a mini-bye. The Packers last played on October 29 on Thursday Night Football. By the time you're reading this, that was 10 days ago. Double-digit days is a long time to go without playing football in the NFL. For the Packers, it was a chance to re-set after a 5-3 start, though. Frankly, it was a much-needed re-set, and hopefully it will have done this team well. There's still extremely injured and maddeningly inconsistent on this side of the mini-bye, but Jordan Love is playing like a potential MVP candidate , Jonathan Gannon's defense looks really good and oh...Micah Parsons is getting back to practice. That's right, the multi-time All-Pro is getting back to it, though he's not making any promises regarding his level of play. He's also likely not to be activated until the night before Thanksgiving, so he wont' play a role in this one. That is a shame, because the Packers are on the road against one of the better teams in the AFC in the 5-3 Patriots. Here's everything (else) you need to know about this game. Tight end Hunter Henry is hopeful that he'll play, but he was limited in practice on Friday and did not practice earlier in the week. Running back TreVeyon Henderson is scarily dealing with neurological symptoms . With all that firepower hampered, the Patriots are relaying on former 2023 sixth-round pick DeMario Douglas to fuel their offense. Douglas is having the best season of his career so far, with 26 catches for 332 yards and four touchdowns, but he's not the type of player the Pack will lose sleep game planning against. In the meantime, Packers' rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse was the NFL's defensive rookie of the month after recording 21 tackles, seven passes defended, one interception and one sack in October. picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. away.headline: Patriots vs. Packers takeaways: Jordan Love, Christian Watson lead dominant Green Bay performance
away.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Jordan Love (372 yards passing and four total touchdowns), Christian Watson (171 yards receiving and a touchdown) and Matthew Golden (164 yards receiving and a touchdown) tore up the Patriots' secondary all day long. Much of Golden's damage came against Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, the NFL's highest-paid cornerback. Green Bay's defense also shined with four turnovers forced-- three interceptions of Drake Maye and a forced fumble out of Rhamondre Stevenson's hands. Yes, the Packers aren't without warts, but they have what it takes to win the NFC North. The division-leading Minnesota Vikings (6-1) do have the league's best defense across numerous metrics, but the Packers lead the NFL with 19 takeaways. Against Maye on Sunday, Green Bay produced 11 unblocked pressures, the second most in a game this season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. The Packers now lead the NFL with 43 unblocked pressures, the most in the NFL, and that's without All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons. Parsons is set to return in a couple weeks against the Los Angeles Rams. Green Bay pressured Maye on 51.2% of his dropbacks on Sunday, the highest pressure rate of his career in the regular season. The Packers nearly matched the 52.8% pressures rate the Seahawks hit against him in the Super Bowl last season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. Minnesota also has a big quarterback issue with Kyler Murray not fitting into coach Kevin O'Connell's scheme through the first half of the season. Their record could also begin to level out as they play the NFL's toughest schedule from Weeks 8-11. The Detroit Lions needed a buzzer-beater field goal and questionable calls to defeat Green Bay in Detroit in Week 20-17 in Week 7. They face the Packers again in Week 18. Green Bay already beat the Chicago Bears 31-7 in Week 5, and even though Chicago was without Caleb Williams that day, the Bears were the betting favorites at Lambeau Field that day. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love found wide receiver Savion Williams, a 2025 third-round pick out of TCU, in the back left corner of the end zone for the 10-yard touchdown on third down. He is now up to 270 yards passing and 2 two passing touchdowns on 16 of 21 passing, in addition to a 13-yard rushing touchdown, one drive into the second half. The Packers are back up 17, 31-14, with 10:51 left in the third quarter. The New England Patriots needed just four plays to travel 64 yards down the field for a touchdown. All 64 yards came from Drake Maye's right arm as he completed throws of 9 yards, 28 yards, 19 yards and 8 eight yards. The last throw was a floater of a touchdown pass from eight yards out to wide receiver Efton Chism. New England trails by 10, 24-14, with 2:42 left in the first half. away.blurb: Packers list three questionable, rule out five vs. Patriots | Week 9 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Keisean Nixon, two running backs questionable for Sunday Emma Pravecek, packers.com CB Keisean Nixon GREEN BAY – The Packers have listed cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and running backs MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and Chris Brooks (ankle) as questionable for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. "It's always concerning when a guy doesn't practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur on Friday morning. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. Rhyan hasn't practiced since injuring his ankle four snaps into the Packers' Week 7 game in Detroit. Receiver Christian Watson (ribs), guard Aaron Banks (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (personal) didn't receive game statuses and will be available Sunday. Watson broke a rib during the Packers' 27-19 win over Carolina but returned to finish the game. He wore protective padding while practicing in a limited capacity this week. Predicting the Raiders' Week 9 Moves In their Week 8 matchup against the Jets, Las Vegas made several notable changes to their starting lineup that proved fruitful. After struggling to find competent play at the right guard position between Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers, the Raiders turned to rookie Trey Zuhn. The Jets are not known for being a stout defense, but they are serviceable and gave Las Vegas fits for the entire first half, holding the Raiders to 97 total yards. Still, Zuhn looked like he may be the Raiders' best option at right guard for the rest of the season. Sunday's matchup against the 49ers will be much more telling, as San Francisco's defense is much more of a challenge than New York's. It will be interesting to see how Zuhn does at guard against one of the toughest teams the Raiders will face this season. If Zuhn plays well against the 49ers, the starting right guard position is his to lose. Starting Zuhn at right guard wasn't the only change Las Vegas made against the Jets. They also started rookie running back Mike Washington over Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders cannot afford to sit Jeanty for an entire game, as he is far too valuable catching the ball out of the backfield. Still, the way they successfully used Washington on the ground and Jeanty through the air against the Jets is worth building upon in Week 9 against the 49ers. He wants to get better at each and every single thing he does, whether it’s fitting his hands up, his eyes, everything coming out. It’s all the little fundamental things that we talk about. It’s stuff that he wants to get better at, improve on, and that’ll allow him to become a more successful player,” Janocko said earlier this week. “Running the ball is a full team thing. The greatest thing about football in general is that it’s 11 as one on every single play. So, it takes all 11 for everybody to be successful." Cornerback Darien Porter returned to practice this week after playing only one play against the New York Jets last Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable heading into Week 9. However, speed is arguably Porter's greatest asset on the field, and he is dealing with a groin injury. A groin injury can linger. Despite being listed as questionable, Kubiak and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard may decide not to risk damage to Porter's long-term health in a game where they already face an uphill battle. Las Vegas faced a similar decision earlier this season, when they could have rested running back Ashton Jeanty against a New England Patriots team that was missing more than five players before their matchup ended. The Raiders need Porter beyond just this week. Resting Porter on Sunday is far from ideal for Sunday's game, but may be best for his career, depending on the severity of his injury and how much progress he made on it during the week. Porter sitting out would offer a valuable opportunity to other corners on the roster. Porter may very well start against the 49ers. Regardless, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses is sure to see significant playing time. Heading into Sunday, Masses could be in for another action-packed day, who has had extreme highs and lows during this season. “I think it’s always a moving target. See where your team’s at, and who’s playing the best ball at the time. And it’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. And [there have] been changes at guard," Kubiak said earlier this week. "[We have] changed up front defensively. Changed at corner, and that’s the NFL. We have a young roster, and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best." Charlie Disturco · Action Network Sun, November 8, 2026 at 8:23 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) battle the San Francisco 49ers (6-1) today in NFL Week 9. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET from Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The 49ers are 8.5-point favorites on the spread, with the over/under set at 51.5 total points. San Francisco is a -440 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Las Vegas is a +340 underdog. Let's get into my Raiders vs 49ers predictions and player props . Raiders vs. 49ers Picks: Ashton Jeanty Over 27.5 Rushing Yards | Christian McCaffrey Over 60.5 Rushing Yards My Raiders vs. 49ers best bets are two props for Ashton Jeanty and Christian McCaffrey — both overs on their rushing yards. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Raiders vs 49ers Odds Raiders vs 49ers Spread : Raiders +8.5 (-108), 49ers -8.5 (-112) Raiders vs 49ers Total : 51.5 (-118o / -102u) Raiders vs 49ers Moneyline : Raiders +340, 49ers -440 Raiders vs 49ers Preview It seemed like Fernando Mendoza was primed to take over the starting quarterback job as the Raiders spiraled into a four-game losing streak. But a collapse by the Jets kept Kirk Cousins in the driver's seat, and the veteran is expected to start again on Sunday. Despite the Raiders putting up 38 points, one storyline stole the headlines: Mike Washington Jr. handled 25 carries. Ashton Jeanty? Just two. Could that be tied to Jeanty's comments about the Jets' lack of interest in tackling in the week leading up to the game? Possibly. But Jeanty has also been largely inefficient, averaging just 2.2 yards per carry over the previous three weeks. The soft benching could serve as a wake-up call for Jeanty, although Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak still expects the workload split between Jeanty and Washington to vary week to week. I expect Jeanty to get a much larger share of the carries today. Washington didn't exactly make the most of his opportunity, averaging just 3.3 yards per carry on 25 attempts against New York. Despite a struggling run game, Cousins has kept the offense competitive. The Raiders rank sixth in the NFL in scoring at 27.6 points per game, with much of that production going through tight end Brock Bowers , who is averaging 91.2 receiving yards per game. Tre Tucker has emerged as a reliable receiving option thanks to his speed, but the rest of the wide receiver room remains thin. Jalen Nailor has gradually settled into the WR2 role, while Jack Bech continues to work his way back from injury. Defensively, the Raiders can't stop a nosebleed. Opponents have scored at least 30 points against Las Vegas in each of the last five weeks. The Raiders rank in the bottom three in both yards allowed per game (381.9) and points allowed per game (28.8). The 49ers' Week 8 bye came at the perfect time as they continue to deal with one of the most injury-riddled offenses in football. After opening the season with six straight wins, San Francisco fell to Atlanta. Christian McCaffrey battled through an injury and missed a large portion of the game, while the 49ers were also without Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans . Samuel and Evans are not expected to return Sunday, but the 49ers should get Demarcus Robinson back. McCaffrey also benefits from the extra rest and is good to go — a massive boost for an offense that runs through him. Despite all the injuries, the 49ers' offense continues to hum. Brock Purdy is playing like an MVP candidate, and San Francisco ranks among the league's top five in scoring at 28.1 points per game. However, it's the defense that has taken the biggest step forward this season. Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw have elevated the linebacker group, while the midseason acquisition of DeForest Buckner gives the defensive line another dimension. Nick Bosa , who hasn't played since Week 2, also returns from injury today. Allowing fewer than 20 points per game, San Francisco may finally have the pieces to chase that elusive Super Bowl trophy. When healthy, this team can be a force to be reckoned with. Raiders vs 49ers Player Props, Picks There are two props I like in this one. The first is ugly and comes with plenty of uncertainty, but I'm willing to take the risk. I refuse to believe Klint Kubiak is going to make the same mistake twice and leave Ashton Jeanty behind Mike Washington Jr. on the depth chart. There's plenty of speculation surrounding this team, but Washington is not the answer. In fact, he's tied with Jacoby Brissett in broken tackles this season (one). Jeanty is far more explosive than Washington, particularly as a pass catcher. Has the Raiders' run game been a problem all season? Absolutely. But Jeanty's rushing yards prop set at 27.5 is simply too low for me to pass up. I'll hold my nose and back Jeanty, even with the Raiders entering as double-digit underdogs. The second prop centers around Christian McCaffrey. As always, the biggest concern with the superstar is injury risk. However, McCaffrey is coming off a bye week and got Wednesday off, which is standard treatment for many veteran players. He returned to practice Thursday and practiced in full on Friday. The Raiders' run defense has been putrid. We just saw Braelon Allen average 7.0 yards per carry against them last week, marking the seventh consecutive week an opponent has rushed for at least 100 yards. Las Vegas is currently allowing 5.31 yards per carry. Not only should the 49ers have plenty of success against this defense, but the game script could also lead to a more run-heavy approach. McCaffrey is averaging 4.6 yards per carry and has cleared this rushing yards line (60.5) in all five games in which he's played at least 55% of the snaps. Expect a fresher McCaffrey and plenty of success on the ground.
