away.headline: Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism
away.blurb: On Wednesday, the official injury report listed defensive tackles Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi and tight end Ian Thomas as limited participants. Cornerback Darien Porter missed Wednesday's practice with a groin injury he suffered against the Jets. On Thursday, Las Vegas' injury report remained minimal. Porter returned to practice on Thursday, which is good news for the Raiders' young defensive backfield. He was a limited participant, and Thomas was a full participant. Booker did not practice on Thursday. Dont'e Thornton was limited as well. Raiders' Thursday Injury Report Gives Reason for Cautious Optimism Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders are just a few days away from facing the San Francisco 49ers on the road. Las Vegas went back to work on Thursday, looking to build upon their Week 9 win over the New York Jets. Las Vegas' success this season has largely depended on the quality of the opponent they face. The Raiders have played well enough to beat four of the league's worst teams, but have struggled against the league's elite, which the 49ers are. Still, those four wins are more than the Raiders had all last season, and they are unquestionably better than last season. It may have been against the Jets, but Las Vegas aims to translate its second-half success against New York to this Sunday against the 49ers. After struggling in the third quarter all season, the Raiders' offense exploded against the Jets. In Week 8, Kirk Cousins led the Raiders downfield to score on their first offensive drive after halftime for the first time all season. It was more than impactful, as it led to Las Vegas producing their best third quarter of the season. The Raiders must continue to play well on offense to help their defense. “I think the first play of the second half might have been the throw to Brock [Bowers], and I thought that was a key play in the game and a great call by our coaches, and that whole drive, to finish that drive, it got us right back in the game, which we needed, very important," Cousins said earlier this week. “If you punt and they go down and score, it could be a whole different story. So, it’s very important, and we’ve got to be really strong in the third quarter the rest of the way. And I felt we have continued, last week in the fourth quarter, continuing to play well in the fourth quarter. But it’s a four-quarter game. You’ve got to do it, all four of them.” Throughout the rest of the season, Las Vegas needs the Cousins who showed up in the third and fourth quarters against the Jets to show up in each of their next three games. Moving forward, they will need that version of Cousins and their offense even before the third quarter. Fatukasi was a full participant as well. Based on their injury report, Las Vegas appears to be the healthiest it has been this season, as their Week 1 injury report listed stars Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers. The Raiders will likely give rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses a bigger role

home.headline: Another 49ers receiver added to injury report ahead of Week 9 vs. Raiders
home.blurb: SANTA CLARA — The 49ers continued to see several of their players return to the field following the bye week, but there also was a new absence. Christian Kirk , who was limited on Wednesday with a knee injury, did not participate in Thursday's practice. The veteran wideout was on the field for 20 offensive snaps in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons after being sidelined with a calf injury at the start of training camp. 49ers expect two players to return from injury, hit practice field on Wednesday Standout special teams players Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford both were back on the field for a second consecutive practice. The two linebackers’ absences were felt in the 49ers' Week 7 loss to the Falcons, when return coverage was clearly challenged. Christian Kirk added to 49ers injury report before Week 9 game – NBC Sports Bay Area & California Warriors Yet another 49ers receiver was added to the injury report ahead of San Francisco's Week 9 game vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. By Jennifer Lee Chan • Published November 5, 2026 • Updated on November 5, 2026 at 2:49 pm Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans were both absent for a second practice ahead of the team's Week 9 clash with the Las Vegas Raiders. Demarcus Robinson , however, participated in his second straight practice after missing substantial time with a high ankle sprain. The expectation is that Robinson will be ready for Sunday's game. Nick Bosa was seen on the field for a second consecutive session after missing five games with a calf injury in the leg, and did not suffer the ACL injury in Week 3 of the 2025 season. The All-Pro warmed up alongside DeForest Buckner , who likely will play a sizable role on Sunday. Upton Stout , who has been wearing a blue non-contact jersey, was seen in his standard No. 20 jersey, indicating that he could be healthy enough to play on Sunday. After being sidelined on Wednesday with a hamstring injury, Christian McCaffrey returned to the field, along with Trent Williams , who had a veteran rest day. TOP PICK Cardinals vs Seahawks prediction: Over 38.5 The Over 38.5 sits at 52% , and while nobody expected a Gardner Minshew vs. Drew Lock battle two weeks ago, it sets us up for a high-scoring game. Lock threw three touchdown passes in Week 2 when these teams met, finishing with a 139.1 QB rating, as the Seattle Seahawks scored 31 points. With Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet returning last week, their ground game improved, as did their pass protection, which will help Lock. A week of practice puts Minshew in a strong position after a sensational cameo last week. He added some much-needed juice to this offense, throwing three touchdowns. His 75% completion percentage on passes of 20+ yards was a huge increase from Jacoby Brissett , who had averaged 20.7% across the season. Cardinals vs Seahawks combo We don't know exactly how healthy Lock is, given he's been inactive for two weeks, which limits my optimism about backing the Seahawks. The return of their starting running backs is big, but the blocking hasn't helped, and the team ranks 29th overall in EPA/rush. Conversely, the Arizona Cardinals ' ground game is in rude health, ranking 10th in EPA/rush. The Cardinals' defense is also improving, allowing 5.02 yards per play across the past two games , a drop of more than one yard from the 6.18 it allowed in Weeks 1-5. Jaxon Smith-Njigba remains the Seahawks' main threat and is QB-proof. He's scored nine times this season, four of them with Lock at QB, and has the sixth-most red-zone targets of any WR. Cardinals +9.5 Jaxon Smith-Njigba anytime touchdown Cardinals vs Seahawks touchdown scorer: Trey McBride The Seahawks have allowed only two touchdowns to tight ends, but Trey McBride isn't a normal TE, and this is a good spot for him. He has five touchdowns this season, including one against the Seahawks in Week 2, and has found the end zone in each of his past two games. He also leads the entire NFL in red-zone targets with 19 and has 10 targets inside the 10-yard line . The QB change shouldn't impact him much either, given that Minshew targeted him eight times on 23 passing attempts. I'd play this up to 35%. During his time on the field, Allgeier managed three runs of 10+ yards, more than 25% of the 11 that the entire offense had made all season up until that point. away.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: Report
away.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. away.headline: Cardinals Forced to Sign 40-Year-Old QB as Injuries Mount
away.source: Arizona Cardinals On SI on MSN
away.blurb: “I think probably even stronger than how I said it yesterday. I wasn’t anticipating some of the things that we found out today. I knew that particularly on offense — (with) the defense there’s been a guy here and there, but there’s been some decent continuity over the last month, and I think you guys see that," LaFleur said. Cardinals Coach Said The Quiet Part Out Loud on Carson Beck ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' Monday has taken a steep twist thanks to several significant injuries to their offense, and with news of Gardner Minshew potentially being done for the season, the organization has already targeted their next passer. From ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter: "With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons." Johnson, a perennial backup veteran quarterback, will be the team's No. 2 quarterback as the Cardinals prepare for their Week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams — who just welcomed Myles Garrett back to the mix with a three-sack performance this Sunday. Minshew was injured on the final play of the second quarter against Seattle. He returned to finish the game but showed obvious discomfort. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck is slated to start for Arizona this week. Johnson, 40 years old, first entered the league as a fifth-round pick in the 2008 NFL Draft. He's played 50 NFL games with 11 starts, most recently starting twice for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, Johnson completed 34 of 54 passes for 372 yards for one touchdown and two interceptions. He has a 2-9 record as a starter. It was an extremely tough day for the Cardinals, who lost both Minshew and Michael Wilson . Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur says the team has to regroup, even amid the injuries. "I think you see 11 has won more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now and that’s what I meant by that. There’s been a lot of moving parts, and I have to do a better job of stabilizing that to make sure that we don’t have performances like we did yesterday.” The Cardinals recently dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens last week, thinning their quarterback room down to two. With Minshew injured, Beck was the only healthy quarterback on the roster prior to Johnson's signing. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals face quarterback crisis as Gardner Minshew faces potential season-ending injury
away.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur addressed the media on Monday, confirming that Minshew is scheduled for an MRI to determine the full extent of the damage. While the team has not officially ruled the quarterback out for the year, the organization is already preparing for a transition under center. Reports indicate that rookie Carson Beck is the primary candidate to assume the starting responsibilities should Minshew be placed on the sidelines for an extended period. The Arizona Cardinals are confronting a significant roster challenge following reports that starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II has sustained a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing arm. The injury, which occurred during Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, has raised concerns that the 30-year-old signal-caller may be sidelined for the remainder of the season. The incident took place on the final play of the first half when Minshew was struck while being sacked. Despite the severity of the injury, Minshew returned to the field for the third quarter and completed the game. Following the contest, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the quarterback is undergoing further medical evaluations, with initial assessments suggesting a recovery period that could span several months. Transition to Rookie Leadership and Roster Adjustments Beck’s path to the starting lineup was cleared earlier this week when the Cardinals traded veteran Jacoby Brissett, effectively elevating the rookie to the backup position. Although Beck has yet to make his regular-season debut, he saw significant action during the preseason Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers, where he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. His development was previously hindered by a rib injury, but his recent promotion has increased his involvement in team practices. To bolster the quarterback room, the Cardinals are reportedly moving to sign veteran Josh Johnson from the Cleveland Browns' practice squad. The addition of Johnson provides the team with necessary depth as they navigate the uncertainty surrounding Minshew’s status and prepare for the upcoming stretch of the season. home.headline: ‘They Didn’t Have To Tell Us That,’ ‘Definitely Unusual’ — NFL Analyst Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Reveal Sam Darnold’s Surprise Injury
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. home.headline: Injury Report: Week 9 vs Seahawks
home.blurb: A decision on the status of defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle), right guard Isaiah Adams (ankle), and cornerback Max Melton (knee) will be made closer to the game. They are listed as questionable. If the Cardinals think Adams could play, he will need to be activated by Saturday afternoon. Seattle will be without Sam Darnold (quadricep/rib) as they turn to Drew Lock for the third time this season. They ruled out recently acquired offensive guard Quenton Nelson (knee), starting left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee), linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), and defensive lineman Leonard Williams (stinger). Walter Nolen continues to practice in a limited capacity, but the Cardinals defensive lineman took a step forward on Thursday. Nolen was working off to the side during drills when practice started this week, but he was back working with the defensive lineman during the open portion of practice. It was another limited practice for Isaiah Adams, who could potentially return to the starting lineup with a good and healthy week of work. Running back Bam Knight (concussion) and right guard Jon Gaines II (ankle) did not practice. Game designations come out on Friday. The Seahawks added linebackers Derick Hall (back) and Ernest Jones (ankle) to the injury report. Recently acquired offensive guard, Quenton Nelson, was downgraded to a DNP after being limited on Wednesday with a knee injury. Also returning to practice on Wednesday was Walter Nolen III. The defensive tackle is working through an ankle injury and was limited. The Cardinals were without left tackle Jayden Williams, who exited the Cowboys game with a knee injury. Josh Fryar would become the third player to start at left tackle if Williams can't go. Running back Bam Knight did not practice because of his concussion. Rest days sidelined safety Budda Baker, outside linebacker Josh Sweat, left guard Isaac Seumalo, and center Hjalte Froholdt. Wide receiver Michael Wilson was wearing the yellow non-contact uniform and was limited. Kickoff is set for 8:20 p.m. ET from Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. The game will broadcast live on NBC. The Bears are 6.5-point favorites over the Buccaneers on the spread, with the over/under set at 47.5 total points. Chicago is a -270 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tampa Bay is a +220 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Buccaneers vs Bears predictions for Sunday Night Football . Buccaneers vs Bears pick: Buccaneers +6.5 (-120) My Buccaneers vs. Bears best bet is Tampa Bay to cover the spread, with the best price currently available at FanDuel . Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Buccaneers vs Bears Odds Buccaneers vs Bears spread: Buccaneers +6.5 (-120), Bears -6.5 (+100) Buccaneers vs Bears total: over/under 47.5 (-110o / -110u) Buccaneers vs Bears moneyline: Buccaneers +220, Bears -270 Buccaneers vs Bears Sunday Night Football Preview Tampa Bay Buccaneers Betting Preview We have another intriguing NFC primetime matchup on our hands tonight with the red-hot Bears hosting the surging Buccaneers . That may sound familiar because the Bears will be playing in primetime for the third straight week. That's pretty uncommon. For what it's worth, since 2003, teams playing their third consecutive primetime have gone 16-20 ATS. The past two victories have come against last year's Super Bowl participants with their most recent coming against Seattle with extra time to prepare. This situation is a little trickier since the Bears will be traveling back from Seattle on a short week, which can only be a positive for Tampa. The less time you give Ben Johnson to prepare for an opponent, the better, if you're that opponent. The Bucs have won two straight games in blowout fashion to get right back in the thick of the NFC South race. They've done so despite Baker Mayfield only completing seven total passes, including a grand total of zero last week in a monsoon against Atlanta. The Bucs became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass. That does make this handicap a little trickier since we really don't know if his previous thumb injury will be an issue when he has to throw more frequently, which he certainly will need to do tonight. Tampa has ridden its running game, spearheaded by Bucky Irving, and defense during its recent surge. Coming into this week, the Bucs ranked first overall in Defensive DVOA with no glaring holes in their analytical profile. In fact, they actually rank in the top-2 in both drop back and rushing EPA. Todd Bowles has this unit playing at an elite level at the moment, which will create a strength on strength matchup when the Bears have the ball. Chicago Bears Betting Preview There's not much more you can say about the Bears offense at the moment. You could argue it's the best in the NFL with a healthy Caleb Williams , who has seemingly taken a massive leap in the second year of Ben Johnson's offense. He's playing within the structure of the scheme, while also still sprinkling in those off-script explosive plays when things break down. Throw in a dominant ground game and this offense has juggernaut potential. The Chicago defense does have some holes. After all, the Bears are only one of two teams that have allowed six or more yards per play (along with the Raiders ). However, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen does seemingly have a good feel for this group and has been dialing up pressures at all the right times. Plus, this unit should continue to trend up following the addition of Jeffery Simmons and a now healthy Kyler Gordon , who Allen will blitz off the edge to generate some of that aforementioned pressure. It's never going to be an elite defense and there is likely some harsh third-down regression looming on the horizon. Chicago leads the NFL on those late downs by a wide margin at an insane 23.75%. Only one other team in the league has allowed a sub-30% and it's Minnesota at 29.75%. However, as long as Chicago's offense stays heathy and Ben Johnson is on the sidelines, it doesn't need its defense to be elite. Just not a total disaster and this is a true Super Bowl contender. Buccaneers vs Bears Prediction, Betting Analysis I like the Bucs here at +6 or better. I mentioned that potential third-down regression, but I also believe the Bucs will have success on the ground here in a game that might not have a ton of possessions, which makes the road pup a bit more intriguing. I have to imagine it's tough to get up emotionally for three straight primetime games, especially on a short week with travel after beating last year's conference winners. I wouldn't be totally surprised if the Bears were just a tad flat or off in the beginning parts of this game. While I don't think Tampa's defense can completely shut down Chicago's offense, the Buccaneers are playing as well as anybody in the league on that side of the ball at the moment. Even if I adjust for schedule, I have the Bucs rated as a top-3 defense this season — and in order to have a prayer against a Ben Johnson offense, you have to be stout against the run. Tampa has certainly fit that profile for years under Bowles and does so once again this season (second in rush DVOA). I'm selling high on the Bears and taking the six points with Baker and the boys. picks.blurb: Prediction For Buccaneers' Sunday Night Showdown With the Chicago Bears - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire Prediction For Buccaneers' Sunday Night Showdown With the Chicago Bears (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have shown everyone what they are capable of over the last two games. The Bucs have beaten the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons , a pair of NFC South rivals, by a combined score of 59-13 in the last two weeks to pull within a half-game of first place in the division. Now they must show they are capable of beating one of the NFL's top teams when they go on the road to take on the 6-2 Chicago Bears on Sunday night. The Bears are on a much different level than either the Panthers or the Falcons, and the Bucs will need to bring their A-game if they want to pull off the upset. If Tampa Bay can earn what would be its signature victory of the season, it will send a message to the rest of the NFC that the Bucs are for real and not to be taken lightly. If the Bucs lose, it will once again cast doubts over what their ceiling is this season. With the NFL's trade deadline coming up on Tuesday, how the Bucs fare against the Bears is likely to have a big impact on the organization's decision to be buyers or sellers. There are several players the Bucs could target at the deadline who could help them make a playoff push. Tampa Bay also has a few veterans who could fetch valuable draft picks if the team decides to sell. Sunday night's clash features the two best rushing offenses in the NFL. The Bucs average over 168 yards per game on the ground, while the Bears average over 150. Chicago leads the league with 17 rushing touchdowns. The first two of my five keys to a Buccaneers' victory are that the Bucs must stay committed to their running game and stop the Bears from running wild. Tampa has the NFL's stingiest rush defense but will have its hands full against the Bears. Last week, Chicago sent two first-round draft picks to the Tennessee Titans for stud defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who has already taken the defense to a new level. Simmons is a game-changer for the Bears, and his presence will make it much harder for Tampa's offense to find success on the ground. Or through the air. That is, if the Bucs even try to move the ball through the air. Last week, the Bucs became the first NFL team in over 50 years to win a game without completing a pass. The Bears aren't the Falcons. To beat Chicago, Tampa must have a more balanced attack. The Bears' passing offense, on the other hand, is elite. QB Caleb Williams may be the MVP favorite, if not for a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. The Bears have surrounding Williams with weapons. Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze give Chicago a dynamic WR duo. Colston Loveland is one of the best and most dangerous tight ends in the NFL. Tampa cornerbacks Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish have played lights out all season and will once again have to step up against a terrific passing attack. This game will have serious playoff implications for the Bucs and could be the difference in whether the organization buys or sells at the deadline. Marching into Chicago and marching out with a win is a tough task for any team, especially one that seems to have only half an offense like the Bucs. I think the Bucs keep things close all game, but the Bears always seem to be just out of reach throughout. Prediction: Bears 30, Bucs 19

picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for the Bears against the Buccaneers
picks.blurb: 3 bold predictions for the Bears against the Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline tracker Bills beat Vikings on MNF Wemby's on a tear NFL Power Rankings Week 10 Waiver Wire 3 bold predictions for the Bears against the Buccaneers Oct 22, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze (15) | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Casey McAleer · Da Windy City Sun, November 8, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears are 6-2, and they spend Sunday night at home in primetime against a 3-5 Buccaneers. The Bears stand to gain the lead in the NFC North provided they win, and the Minnesota Vikings lose to the Buffalo Bills. That sounds simple enough, but if you've followed this team all season, you know nothing about the Bears is ever simple. As such, here are three bold predictions for Sunday night's game. Luther Burden III goes over 100 yards again Burden put up 130 yards against New England the last time the Bears played in primetime, and he's only taken on more of the offense since then, with 19 catches for 281 yards and two touchdowns in the three games since Caleb Williams returned to the field. Tampa Bay has to commit bodies to stopping the run, because that's what every team has to do against Chicago under Ben Johnson. When that happens, it must open up someone on the outside, and that someone has been Burden. Rome Odunze finally scores a touchdown Odunze has been a good receiver for Williams, posting 28 receptions, 468 yards, and a team best 16.7 yards per catch. But through eight weeks this season, he has still yet to scratch a touchdown. Coach Johnson keeps scheming Odunze open, the chances keep coming, but for whatever reason, it hasn't been in the cards yet. On Sunday night, in front of the national audience, the most due touchdown must finally happen. Jeffery Simmons breaks the ground war The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took the crown as the best rushing team in the NFL from the Bears only last week, after they posted a franchise record of 324 rushing yards against the Atlanta Falcons. The Bears only recently traded two first round picks to go and get Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, and he's made an immediate impact. In his Bears debut, Simmons recorded six tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss, and a pass defended. The bold call is two sacks from Simmons, and he'll help to hold the Buccaneers to under 100 rushing yards. If the Bears can hit all three of these bold predictions, they'll be in a very good position to win this game and potentially take first place in their division. But if none of these three things happen, the Bears may just fall into their own trap. | More Bears on DaWindyCity | Riq Woolen comments on potential trade shouldn't change Bears deadline plans Luther Burden III's concussion comes with a single silver lining Austin Booker's ascension should change Bears' trade deadline plans Rome Odunze finally found the end zone Tonight, Bears fans are Bills fans This article was originally published on www.dawindycity.com as 3 bold predictions for the Bears against the Buccaneers .

home.headline: Chicago Bears: Luther Burden suffers concerning injury in Week 9 win
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears eked out a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9. But the franchise isn’t fully celebrating. Wide receiver Luther Burden suffered a concussion in the victory, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. He will now have the bye week to rest up before potentially returning in Week 11. First, Burden will need to pass the NFL’s concussion protocol. Having the extra week will help, but every player and injury is different. Chicago will be paying close attention to their rising wide receiver. The Bears have plenty of talented pass catchers on their roster. But losing Burden for an extended period of time would be a massive blow . Chicago Bears can’t afford Luther Burden loss Against the Buccaneers, Burden led the team with seven receptions for 97 yards and a touchdown. He has been on a tear as of late, scoring a touchdown in three-straight games. When quarterback Caleb Williams drops back to pass, Burden is one of the first targets he is looking for. Speaking of targets, the receiver hasn’t had fewer than four all season. And in the game he did have four, Burden still turned that into 130 yards and a touchdown. Following Week 9, the playmaker has now caught 49 passes for 644 yards and four touchdowns. He leads the Bears in all three categories. And with nine more receiveing yards, Burden will set new career-highs across the board. Based on his recent play, it’s safe to assume the wide receiver would hit that mark in Week 9 barring a true lockdown performance from the New Orleans Saints. But of course, the pass catcher needs to be on the gridiron to truly leave his mark. The Bears will have further updates once Burden undergoes more tests. Once the Week 11 injury reports start rolling around, Chicago will know where their receiver stands. Want more articles like this? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Josh Allen and Buffalo's explosive offense face Brian Flores' dominant defense, while Carson Wentz replaces the injured Kyler Murray Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Minnesota Vikings host the Buffalo Bills . Minnesota is coming off its first loss of the season after starting the year with six straight wins. The Vikings turn to Carson Wentz to start in place of Kyler Murray , who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Minnesota sports arguably the NFL's best defense, and it will be put to the test on Monday night against the Bills. Buffalo has won three consecutive games to improve to 6-1, and last week beat up on the Baltimore Ravens following an injury to Lamar Jackson on the Ravens' first snap of the game. Buffalo is in first place in the AFC East behind its efficient and explosive offense, which has helped offset a defense that has been highly vulnerable this year. Will the Vikings bounce back, or will the Bills continue to roll? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. How to watch Vikings vs. Bills live Date: Monday, Nov. 9 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: U.S. Bank Stadium (Minneapolis) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -3, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bills have the ball This is going to be one of the most fascinating matchups of the season, as arguably the NFL's best quarterback ( Josh Allen ) will do battle with arguably the NFL's best defensive play-caller (Brian Flores). We know the state of play: the Vikings are going to blitz on damn near every snap, and the Bills are going to have to figure out how in the world to deal with all the extra bodies the Vikings send against both the run and the pass. Last week, the Vikings totally shut down one of the best offenses in the league during the first half, holding the Lions to a mere 154 total yards (on 36 plays, an average of 4.3 per play) and only six points prior to the break. They frustrated Jared Goff and the passing game with their heavy blitzing and they limited Jahmyr Gibbs and company to a 25% rushing success rate. Buffalo has been one of the best running teams in the NFL, averaging 4.8 yards per carry, which ranks fourth in the league. The Bills can lean on James Cook, who, after leading the NFL in rushing last year, is actually averaging nearly six more rushing yards per game than he did a year ago. Buffalo likes to get downhill runs with schemes like duo that create double teams inside, which is tough to do against the Vikings, but can lead to big gains if you can block them up front. Whether the Bills can do that is obviously another question. It's important to note that Allen has been blitzed on exactly a third of his dropbacks, per Tru Media, meaning he's faced the 11th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. He's 46 of 70 for 587 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions on those plays, and he's been sacked six times. That's all led to him checking in fourth in yards per attempt (8.4) and seventh in passing success rate (50.0%) but only 15th in EPA per dropback thanks to the interceptions. The Bills will need to get the ball out quickly against the blitz, which could mean underneath targets like Khalil Shakir and passing-down back Ty Johnson are heavily involved. It might be a lighter game for the likes of Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox , as teams often keep their tight ends back in pass protection against Flores' blitz-happy defense. It might also be tough for DJ Moore and Keon Coleman to get open down the field, but there could be opportunities for big plays if the offensive line does hold up on any given snap. The Vikings have given up the occasional deep shot this year because they send so many men after the quarterback and it leaves them shorthanded on the back end at times. When the Vikings have the ball The Vikings have struggled to move the ball pretty much all season. Their 4.7 yards-per-play average is tied for third-worst in the NFL. Their 1.71 points-per-drive average is fifth-worst in the NFL. And their -0.14 expected points added per play average is second-worst in the NFL, according to Tru Media. They've yet to gain more than 364 yards in any game, and they've been at 275 or fewer in five of their seven contests. They've scored more than 23 points just one time, and it was back in Week 1 when they had touchdown drives of 28, 1 and 14 yards late in the game against the Green Bay Packers . Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of Kyler Murray, who has completed 64.9% of his passes at an average of just 6.6 yards per attempt, with a mere five touchdown passes and three interceptions. Some of the struggles can be laid at the feet of the run game, where the backs have combined to average south of 4.0 yards per carry. Jordan Mason missed four games, but it's not like he's been effective when he's been on the field, having averaged 3.9 yards a pop. Murray won't be on the field on Monday night. It'll be Carson Wentz under center in his place. Wentz went 23 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns in one-plus games in relief of Murray earlier this year. He seemed to have more command of the offense and more chemistry with Justin Jefferson than Murray does, at the very least. Jefferson went for eight catches for 92 yards and two scores during Wentz's relief appearance back in Week 1, and he was on the receiving end of seven of Wentz's 19 pass attempts in that game. (Wentz's start the following week came in a driving rainstorm in Chicago and doesn't provide much room for analysis.) If the Vikings can keep Wentz well-protected, there should be some opportunities for Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson to find openings in what has been a very leaky back seven. The Bills have been solid against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry. Given the Vikings' struggles on the ground, it seems unlikely that they'll have much in the way of success running the ball here. You can't ask me to buy into this Minnesota offense right now — not even against Buffalo's leaky defense. We just saw the Vikings put up a relatively limp offensive performance against the Lions. And if there's a team out there that can run the ball on Minnesota the way the Lions did, it might be the Bills with Josh Allen and James Cook. Buffalo can win a low-ish scoring game here by doing just that. away.headline: Bills injury report: Dion Dawkins, Joshua Palmer miss practice again
away.blurb: Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins missed practice for the second straight day Friday because of a rib injury, while right tackle Spencer Brown remained limited with the back injury that kept him out of Sunday's victory over the Baltimore Ravens . Six Buffalo players did not practice Friday, although wide receiver Khalil Shakir was absent for personal reasons and defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. was out with an illness. There was some encouraging news. Tight end Dalton Kincaid returned to full participation after being limited Thursday because of a chest injury, while running back Ty Johnson returned after missing the previous day's practice with an illness. Brown has been limited both days because of a back injury that has bothered him since Buffalo's Week 5 victory over the Los Angeles Rams . The receiver pulled up while running a deep route late in the first quarter. He went to the ground and was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Palmer has already missed time this season because of a shoulder injury that kept him out of Buffalo's Week 5 victory over the Rams. The Bills also listed Keon Coleman as limited for the second consecutive day because of a shoulder injury. D.J. Moore remained limited with the shoulder injury that previously cost him two games. Moore returned against Baltimore but also hyperextended his knee during the fourth quarter. Kincaid was a full participant Friday after being limited Thursday because of a chest injury. The Bills also opened the 21-day practice window for defensive back Jordan Hancock on Thursday. Hancock, who has been on injured reserve since September because of a hamstring injury, remained limited Friday. The Vikings also practiced without wide receiver Jauan Jennings on Friday after he was limited Thursday because of a calf injury. Darrisaw was limited Thursday but returned to full practice Friday. Van Ginkel, who is tied for fifth in the NFL with 6.5 sacks, remained limited with a chest injury. He recorded 2.5 sacks against Detroit on Sunday. Claiborne is currently in his 21-day return-to-practice window. home.blurb: Buffalo's Thursday report includes five players who did not participate in practice, while five were limited and eight were full participants. The list also includes defensive back Jordan Hancock, who remains on injured reserve, and wide receiver Tyrell Shavers, who is on the physically unable to perform list. The biggest concern on the offensive line involves left tackle Dion Dawkins and right tackle Spencer Brown. Dawkins did not practice Thursday because of a rib injury, while Brown was limited with a back issue. Both starting tackles will be worth watching as the week progresses. Alec Anderson was also a non-participant with an ankle injury, meaning Buffalo's entire left side of the line was out. Buffalo's receiving group also has a few players dealing with injuries. Joshua Palmer did not practice because of a hamstring injury after leaving Sunday's win over Baltimore, while Keon Coleman was limited with a shoulder issue. DJ Moore, who recently returned from a shoulder injury, was also limited on Thursday and in a red non-contact. The good news, however, is that it was just for his shoulder after appearing to hyperextend his knee in Week 8. Tight end Dalton Kincaid was limited with a chest injury, while running back Ty Johnson missed practice because of an illness. The defensive side of the ball has its own concerns. Defensive tackle Greg Gaines did not practice with a calf injury, and cornerback Dee Alford was listed as a full participant with the ankle injury that kept him out last week. Ed Oliver, meanwhile, was a full participant with a knee injury.
